# Home

<img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/docs/assets/logo.svg" width="72" height="72" alt="">

Swiftshot renders screenshots of the previews you already have, for every device, language and
appearance, from one command: for screenshot tests, and as App Store and Google Play screenshots.

- **iOS**: SwiftUI and UIKit `#Preview`s, for every iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch and iOS version,
  without booting a simulator. Apple silicon Mac with Xcode.
- **Android**: Jetpack Compose `@Preview`s, for phones, foldables, tablets and Wear OS, without an
  emulator. Mac or Linux with a JDK 21+.
- **Compose Multiplatform**: shared `@Preview`s for Android, desktop and iOS in one run. Linux
  renders the Android and desktop targets.
- **Flutter**: widget `@Preview`s for iPhones, iPads and Android devices. Mac or Linux; on a Mac
  with Xcode, iOS renders on Flutter's iOS engine, pixel identical to a simulator.

Run `swiftshot` in the project folder: an Xcode project renders iOS, a Gradle project Android, a
`pubspec.yaml` Flutter.

**Start here**

- [[Installation]]: install on a Mac, Linux or a CI machine
- [[Android]]: Jetpack Compose previews for phones, foldables, tablets and Wear OS
- [[Compose Multiplatform]]: Android, desktop and iOS screenshots from shared previews
- [[Flutter]]: widget previews on iPhones, iPads and Android devices
- [[Configuration]]: `swiftshot.json` and per-screenshot settings, for every platform
- [[Command line]]: every command and flag
- [[Screenshot testing]]: record a baseline, verify against it, accept changes
- [[Agents]]: for a coding agent: set up, verify, read `result.json`, and what to leave to CI
- [[CI]]: GitHub Actions and other CI systems
- [[Device frames]]: Apple bezels, App Store titles and backgrounds, Android Studio's device art
- [[Migrating|Migrating-from-fastlane]]: from `fastlane snapshot` and `screengrab`, Paparazzi and Roborazzi
- [[How it works]]: why it's fast and how output stays pixel identical
- [[Troubleshooting]]
- [[Roadmap]]: what's planned for upcoming versions

**Links**

- [README](https://github.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot#readme)
- [Releases](https://github.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/releases)
- [GitHub Marketplace](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/swiftshot-preview-screenshots)
- [Report a bug](https://github.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/issues/new/choose)

# Installation

## Requirements

| | iOS | Android, desktop, Compose Multiplatform |
|---|---|---|
| machine | Apple silicon Mac | Mac or Linux (Compose Multiplatform iOS targets need a Mac) |
| tools | Xcode 26.6 or 27.x, and the simulator runtimes you render (Xcode > Settings > Components) | JDK 21 or later; the Android SDK only for Android targets |
| project | an app with `#Preview`s, iOS 17 or later | a Gradle project with Compose `@Preview`s and `ui-tooling` on the debug classpath, see [[Android]] |

Nothing has to be added to either project.

## Homebrew (Mac and Linux)

```
brew install lukasanda/tap/swiftshot
```

The formula lives in [LukasAnda/homebrew-tap](https://github.com/LukasAnda/homebrew-tap)
and is updated on every release. On a Mac it installs both platforms: `swiftshot` renders iOS, and
hands over to the Android renderer in a Gradle project. On Linux it installs the Android renderer
and Homebrew's `openjdk@21`.

## Linux

On Linux `swiftshot` renders Android (Jetpack Compose, Wear OS) and the Android and desktop
targets of Compose Multiplatform. iOS targets are skipped. The commands and `swiftshot.json` are
the same as on a Mac.

| | |
|---|---|
| Homebrew | `brew install lukasanda/tap/swiftshot` |
| Debian, Ubuntu | `curl -fsSLO https://github.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/releases/latest/download/swiftshot_all.deb && sudo apt install ./swiftshot_all.deb` |
| Fedora, RHEL, openSUSE | `sudo dnf install https://github.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/releases/latest/download/swiftshot.noarch.rpm` |
| any distribution | the [install script](#install-script-mac-and-linux), or `swiftshot-android.tar.gz` from the releases page |

The `.deb` recommends `openjdk-21-jre-headless`, the `.rpm` `java-21-openjdk-headless`; any other
JDK 21+ works too ([JDK](#jdk-android)). Each release also has versioned packages,
`swiftshot_<version>_all.deb` and `swiftshot-<version>-1.noarch.rpm`, each with a `.sha256`.

## Install script (Mac and Linux)

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.swiftshot/bin:$PATH"
```

| machine | downloads | installs |
|---|---|---|
| Apple silicon Mac | `swiftshot-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | iOS and Android |
| Linux, Intel Mac | `swiftshot-android.tar.gz` | Android, desktop and Compose Multiplatform (no iOS): a `swiftshot` launcher and its jars |

| variable | default | |
|---|---|---|
| `SWIFTSHOT_VERSION` | latest | release to install, e.g. `0.8.0` |
| `SWIFTSHOT_PREFIX` | `~/.swiftshot` | install location |
| `SWIFTSHOT_ANDROID_ONLY` | | set on an Apple silicon Mac to install the Android package only |

The script downloads from the [releases page](https://github.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/releases) and
checks the SHA-256.

## JDK (Android)

The Android renderer needs a JDK 21 or later. Android Studio's bundled one, and a Linux
distribution's, are found automatically. The first one that exists and is 21 or later is used:

1. `--java-home` or `"java_home"` in `swiftshot.json`
2. `SWIFTSHOT_JAVA_HOME`
3. `JAVA_HOME`
4. Android Studio's JDK: `/Applications/Android Studio.app`, `~/Applications/Android Studio.app`,
   `/opt/android-studio/jbr`
5. `java` on `PATH`
6. `/usr/lib/jvm/*`, newest first

Without one, `swiftshot` says which package to install.

`--java-home` applies to the renderer processes and the Gradle build (as `JAVA_HOME`); Gradle
otherwise uses your `JAVA_HOME` as usual.

## From source

```
git clone https://github.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot
cd swiftshot
make install         # Mac: iOS and Android, into /usr/local/bin (PREFIX=… to change)
```

`make android` builds only the Android jars and the launcher into `bin/` (any OS with a JDK 21+);
run `bin/swiftshot-android`.

## Check it

```
swiftshot --version    # swiftshot 0.8.0, or "swiftshot 0.8.0 (android)" in a Gradle project
swiftshot devices      # iOS: installed runtimes and devices; in a Gradle project: Android devices
```

## Update

Homebrew: `brew upgrade swiftshot`, uninstall with `brew uninstall swiftshot`.

`.deb` / `.rpm`: install the new package the same way; uninstall with `sudo apt remove swiftshot`
or `sudo dnf remove swiftshot`.

Install script: run it again. To uninstall, delete `~/.swiftshot`.

Caches can be deleted at any time: `~/Library/Caches/swiftshot` on a Mac,
`~/.cache/swiftshot` on Linux.

# Android

Swiftshot renders Google Play screenshots from your Jetpack Compose `@Preview`s for phones,
foldables, tablets and Wear OS, in every language and appearance, without an emulator. It runs on
a Mac or on Linux (CI).

For Compose Multiplatform modules (Android, desktop and iOS) see [[Compose Multiplatform]].

## Requirements

- JDK 21 or later (Android Studio's bundled one is found automatically)
- An Android app or library module with Compose `@Preview`s
- `androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling` on the debug classpath, as Android Studio's previews need too:

```kotlin
debugImplementation("androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling")
```

- `mavenCentral()` among the project's repositories: Swiftshot's task resolves Paparazzi's
  layoutlib SDK from there

Nothing else is added to the project: Swiftshot adds its Gradle task for its own run only.

## Install

On an Apple silicon Mac, the regular install includes Android support. On Linux: Homebrew, a
`.deb`, an `.rpm` or the install script, see [[Installation]]. On an Intel Mac:

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | sh
export PATH="$HOME/.swiftshot/bin:$PATH"
```

## Quick start

In the folder with `gradlew`:

```
swiftshot init      # writes swiftshot.json: modules, languages, Play devices
swiftshot           # renders everything
open screenshots/screenshots.html
```

`swiftshot list` prints the previews it found, `swiftshot devices` the devices.

## Configuration

`swiftshot.json` uses the same keys as on iOS where they mean the same thing. It is a file of its
own: keys only iOS knows, such as `scheme`, are rejected.

```json
{
  "modules": [":app", ":wear"],
  "devices": ["Pixel 10 Pro", "Pixel 9 Pro Fold", "Pixel 9 Pro Fold (folded)", "Pixel Tablet"],
  "watch_devices": ["Wear OS Large Round"],
  "languages": ["en-US", "de-DE", "ja", "ar"],
  "appearances": ["light", "dark"],
  "font_scales": [1, 1.3],
  "output_directory": "fastlane/metadata/android",
  "layout": "fastlane",
  "screens": [
    { "preview": "Stats", "full_length": true },
    { "preview": "Debug*", "skip": true }
  ]
}
```

| key | default | |
|---|---|---|
| `project_dir` | `.` | the Gradle project |
| `modules` | every Android module | e.g. `[":app", ":wear"]` |
| `variant` | `debug` | build variant |
| `gradle_args` | `[]` | extra Gradle arguments |
| `devices` | Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel Tablet | phones, foldables, tablets (`swiftshot devices`) |
| `watch_devices` | Wear OS Large Round | for Wear OS modules |
| `languages` | `["en-US"]` | BCP 47 tags |
| `appearances` | `["light"]` | `light`, `dark` |
| `font_scales` | `[1]` | e.g. `[1, 1.3, 2]` |
| `previews` | all | names or `*` globs |
| `output_directory` | `screenshots` | |
| `layout` | `swiftshot` | `fastlane`: `<locale>/images/phoneScreenshots/…` for `fastlane supply` |
| `clear_previous_screenshots` | `false` | |
| `html` | `true` | write `screenshots.html`, and `index.html` in a verify report |
| `full_length` | `false` | grow scrolling screens to their whole content |
| `delay` | `0` | seconds to advance the clock before capture |
| `system_ui` | `preview` | status and navigation bars: as `showSystemUi` says, `always`, `never` |
| `frame` | `none` | `plain`: the device around the screenshot, see [[Device frames]] |
| `round_corners` | `black` | outside round watch screens: `black`, `transparent`; Play rejects transparency |
| `android_theme` | the app's theme | window theme for every preview; default: the `<application>` theme in the module's manifest, else Material's |
| `parallel` | from cores and memory | renderer processes: one per core and 1.5 GB, at most 8 |
| `java_home` | | JDK 21+ for Gradle and the renderer |
| `screens` | `[]` | per-screenshot settings, below |

`screens` rules match previews by name or `*` glob, and by fully qualified function when the
pattern has a `.`; the first match wins. Keys: `preview`, `appearances`, `languages`, `devices`, `font_scales`, `full_length`,
`delay`, `skip`, `override_preview` (the rule wins over a preview's own device, size and settings). On
the command line: `--screen "Stats: languages=de-DE,ja devices=Pixel*"`.

## Previews

Each `@Preview` renders as in Android Studio:

- `showSystemUi = true`: the whole screen with the status bar and gesture handle. Apps that
  target API 35 or later are edge-to-edge, as Android enforces: the content gets the system bar
  insets and draws behind them.
- Without it: the composable at its own size (a component).
- `device`, `widthDp`/`heightDp`, `locale`, `uiMode` (dark), `fontScale`: the preview's own value
  wins over the matrix, so `@Preview(device = Devices.PIXEL_TABLET)` renders only on that tablet.
- Multipreviews (`@PreviewLightDark`, `@PreviewScreenSizes`, `@PreviewFontScale`,
  `@WearPreviewDevices`, your own) expand like in the IDE, named `Function - Name`.
- `@PreviewParameter`: one screenshot per value, `Name_1.png`, `Name_2.png`…
- Dialogs, bottom sheets and popups shown in the preview are captured, as real windows.

## Devices

The device list is Android Studio's own catalog, generated into Swiftshot: every Pixel, the
reference phones and tablets, foldables unfolded and folded (`Pixel 9 Pro Fold (folded)` is the
outer screen) and Wear OS round and square screens. Wear OS modules (those using Wear Compose)
render on `watch_devices`, once, dark (Wear OS has no light mode).

## Output

```
<output_directory>/<language>/<device>-<preview>[-<appearance>][-<font scale>x].png
<output_directory>/screenshots.html
<output_directory>/swiftshot-report.json
```

- `-light` / `-dark` when both are rendered, `-dark` also when only dark is. None when the preview
  sets `uiMode` itself, and none on Wear OS.
- `-1.3x` for a font scale other than 1, or when several are rendered.
- `@PreviewParameter` values: `_1`, `_2`… Two previews with the same name: the second gets ` 2`.

With `"layout": "fastlane"`, screenshots go where `fastlane supply` uploads them from, inside
`output_directory` (use `fastlane/metadata/android`):

| device | folder |
|---|---|
| phones | `<locale>/images/phoneScreenshots` |
| tablets and foldables up to 9" | `<locale>/images/sevenInchScreenshots` |
| larger tablets and foldables | `<locale>/images/tenInchScreenshots` |
| Wear OS | `<locale>/images/wearScreenshots` |
| TV | `<locale>/images/tvScreenshots` |

`--frame plain` writes framed copies to `<output_directory>-framed/`, see [[Device frames]].

## CI

Linux runners are enough:

```yaml
jobs:
  screenshots:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with: { distribution: temurin, java-version: 21 }
      - uses: LukasAnda/swiftshot@v0.8.0
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with: { name: screenshots, path: screenshots }
```

More in [[CI]].

## How it works

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  cli["swiftshot"] -->|"init script"| gradle["Gradle<br/>swiftshotPrepare"]
  gradle -->|"classes, classpath,<br/>resources"| scan["@Preview scan<br/>(bytecode)"]
  scan --> plan["matrix<br/>devices × languages ×<br/>appearances × font scales"]
  plan --> r1["renderer 1<br/>layoutlib"]
  plan --> r2["renderer 2<br/>layoutlib"]
  plan --> rn["renderer n<br/>layoutlib"]
  r1 & r2 & rn --> out["PNGs, gallery,<br/>report, frames"]
```

Renderer processes start while Gradle is still building, from the previous run's classpath, and
are kept when it is unchanged.

1. **Build.** Swiftshot runs `./gradlew swiftshotPrepare` with an init script: the variant is
   compiled as usual and the task writes the module's classes, runtime classpath, resources and
   assets to a JSON file. Nothing in the project changes.
2. **Find previews.** `@Preview` is invisible to reflection (binary retention), so Swiftshot reads
   the compiled class files directly, resolving multipreview annotations from the project and its
   libraries.
3. **Render.** Renderer processes load the app's classpath together with layoutlib, the rendering
   engine of Android Studio's previews, through Paparazzi's SDK. Each process starts once and then
   renders whole groups of screenshots (one device, language, appearance and font scale) by
   swapping only the composable. Several processes run in parallel; a class-data-sharing archive
   makes each one start faster after the first run.
4. **System UI.** On a device the status bar and gesture handle are system windows above the app,
   so Swiftshot hands the content real insets and draws the bars over the finished frame.

Paparazzi and Roborazzi run screenshots as unit tests: Gradle compiles a test source set and a
test task renders one screenshot per test, one at a time per JVM. Swiftshot skips the test
machinery and renders in parallel processes that stay up for the whole run.

Coming from Paparazzi or Roborazzi? `swiftshot init` reads their tests and sets each preview to
the devices and settings of its tests. Nothing is removed, see
[[Migrating|Migrating-from-fastlane#paparazzi-and-roborazzi]].

More in [[How it works]].

## Speed

The same 470 screenshots from each tool (the demo app's `:app` previews on a Pixel 10 Pro and a
Pixel Tablet, en-US, de-DE, sk, ar, ja, light and dark), on a free 4-core `ubuntu-latest` runner,
one tool after another, the same number of processes for each
([`bench/android`](https://github.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/tree/main/bench/android)):

| | swiftshot | Paparazzi 2.0.0-alpha05.1 | Roborazzi 1.77.0 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| first run (compiles, renders) | **59.4 s** | 86.8 s | 87.7 s |
| warm run | **36.7 s** | 63.6 s | 70.2 s |

What makes the difference:

- No test source set to compile and no test task: one Gradle task writes a JSON file.
- Renderers start while Gradle builds and render whole groups of screenshots each.
- PNG encoding runs beside the next render, at a fast compression level.
- The project's configuration cache is kept: a warm Gradle step takes about a second.

## Limitations

- `apiLevel` in `@Preview` is ignored: every preview renders with layoutlib's Android version.
- Foldables render flat (no hinge posture), as in Android Studio.
- Android TV and Automotive devices render, but get no system bars.
- `swiftshot frame <dir>` and App Store-style frames are iOS only.

# Compose-Multiplatform

Swiftshot renders the `@Preview`s of a Compose Multiplatform module for Android, desktop and iOS
in one run: Play Store, desktop and App Store screenshots from the same shared code.

## Requirements

- A module with `org.jetbrains.kotlin.multiplatform` and Compose Multiplatform
- Previews in `commonMain` with `androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview`
  (`org.jetbrains.compose.ui:ui-tooling-preview`)
- JDK 21 or later
- Android target: `ui-tooling` on its runtime classpath, as for [[Android]]. With the
  `com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library` plugin:

```kotlin
dependencies {
    "androidRuntimeClasspath"("androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling")
}
```

- iOS target: an Apple silicon Mac with Xcode and an `iosSimulatorArm64()` target
- The Android SDK only for the Android target: `--platforms ios` or `desktop` runs without it

Nothing else is added to the project.

## Quick start

In the folder with `gradlew`:

```
swiftshot --devices "Pixel 10 Pro,Pixel Tablet" \
  --desktop-devices "Desktop 1440×900 @2x" \
  --ios-devices "iPhone 17 Pro Max,iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)" \
  --languages "en-US,ar" --appearances light,dark
```

`swiftshot list` prints the previews per target, e.g. `:shared (android)` and `:shared (desktop)`.

## Targets

| target | renders with | devices |
|---|---|---|
| Android (`android {}` or `androidTarget()`) | layoutlib, as for Android modules | `devices` |
| desktop (the first `jvm()` target) | Compose's `ImageComposeScene` (Skia, headless, no window) | `desktop_devices` |
| iOS (`iosSimulatorArm64()`) | Swiftshot's iOS renderer, no simulator booted | `ios_devices` |

All targets present are rendered. Pick some with `--platforms android,desktop` or
`"platforms": ["android", "ios"]`. On a Mac without Xcode, iOS is skipped with a warning.

On Linux, the Android and desktop targets render as on a Mac. iOS targets are not built:
`Compose Multiplatform iOS targets need a Mac with Xcode; skipped here`. The same
`swiftshot.json`, `ios_devices` included, works on both.

Desktop devices: `Desktop 1280×800`, `Desktop 1366×768`, `Desktop 1440×900`, `Desktop 1920×1080`,
and `@2x` versions of 1280×800, 1440×900 and 1920×1080. Default: `Desktop 1440×900 @2x`.

## Configuration

```json
{
  "modules": [":shared"],
  "platforms": ["android", "desktop", "ios"],
  "devices": ["Pixel 10 Pro", "Pixel Tablet"],
  "desktop_devices": ["Desktop 1440×900 @2x"],
  "ios_devices": ["iPhone 17 Pro Max", "iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)"],
  "ios_versions": ["27.0"],
  "languages": ["en-US", "ar"],
  "appearances": ["light", "dark"],
  "output_directory": "screenshots"
}
```

| key | flag | default |
|---|---|---|
| `platforms` | `--platforms` | every target the module has |
| `desktop_devices` | `--desktop-devices` | Desktop 1440×900 @2x |
| `ios_devices` | `--ios-devices` | iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) |
| `ios_versions` | `--ios` | newest installed |

The other keys are the [[Android]] ones.

## Output

Android and desktop screenshots are named as on [[Android]], iOS ones as on iOS, all in one
`output_directory`, gallery and report. With `"layout": "fastlane"`, desktop screenshots go to
`<locale>/images/desktopScreenshots`.

## How the iOS target works

- Previews are found on the module's JVM target.
- Swiftshot's Gradle init script adds a `SwiftshotHost` framework to the iOS simulator target,
  with a generated Kotlin wrapper per preview (`ComposeUIViewController`).
- Private previews are made internal in copies of the sources; your sources are not changed.
- A small SwiftUI host app gets a `#Preview` per preview and is rendered by the iOS no-boot
  renderer.
- Component previews (no `showSystemUi`) render at the size the desktop renderer measured.

The output is pixel identical to a booted simulator.

## Speed

`Example/MultiplatformDemo`, 9 previews in English and Arabic, on an Apple silicon Mac:

- 90 screenshots (Android phone and tablet, desktop, iPhone and iPad) in 19 s
- iOS alone: 72 screenshots (2 devices × 2 languages × light and dark) in about 17 s, including
  the Kotlin/Native framework link

## Limitations

- iOS needs a Mac with Xcode. Linux renders the Android and desktop targets.

# Flutter

Swiftshot renders the `@Preview`s of a Flutter app for iPhones, iPads and Android devices, in
every language and appearance, from one command. It runs on a Mac or on Linux (CI).

## Requirements

- Flutter 3.35 or later, with widget previews (`package:flutter/widget_previews.dart`)
- `flutter_test` among the dev dependencies (the default for new projects)
- JDK 21 or later, as for [[Android]]
- For exact iPhone and iPad screenshots: a Mac with Xcode and the project's `ios/` folder

Nothing is added to the project. `flutter_localizations`, if the project has it, gives every
language its Material localizations and right-to-left layout.

## Quick start

In the folder with `pubspec.yaml`:

```
swiftshot init      # writes swiftshot.json: languages, devices, light and dark
swiftshot           # renders everything
open screenshots/screenshots.html
```

`init` takes the languages from the gen-l10n ARB files (`arb-dir` in `l10n.yaml`) and picks
iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), Pixel 10 Pro and Pixel Tablet. Or on the command line:

```
swiftshot --devices "iPhone 17 Pro Max,Pixel 10 Pro" \
  --languages "en-US,de,ar" --appearances light,dark
```

`swiftshot list` prints the previews, `swiftshot devices` the devices.

## SDK

Swiftshot uses the first of:

1. `--flutter-root` or `"flutter_root"`
2. `FLUTTER_ROOT`
3. the project's fvm version (`.fvmrc` or `.fvm/flutter_sdk`)
4. `flutter` on the `PATH`

## Previews

```dart
@Preview(name: 'Welcome')
Widget welcome() => const WelcomeScreen();

@Preview(name: 'Habit card', size: Size(360, 120), brightness: Brightness.dark)
Widget habitCard() => HabitCard(habit: Habit.sample);
```

- Public top-level functions, static methods and widget constructors. Private ones are skipped
  with a warning.
- `name`, `size`, `textScaleFactor`, `wrapper`, `theme`, `brightness` and `localizations`.
- `MultiPreview` and your own `Preview` subclasses, with `transform()`.
- Previews are found in `lib/` without building.

A preview with a `size` is a component: it renders at that size, without system bars. Without
one, it fills the device's screen.

## Devices

- iPhones and iPads by their iOS names, with the sizes, scale and safe areas measured on the
  simulator.
- Android phones, foldables and tablets from the [[Android]] catalog.

Default: iPhone 17 Pro Max and Pixel 10 Pro.

## Renderers

**Headless** (Mac and Linux):

- `flutter test` with Impeller (Skia where Impeller isn't available), one process per language.
- Each preview gets its wrapper, theme, size, brightness, text scale and localizations, as in
  Flutter's previewer.
- Full screens get system bars: the Android status bar and gesture handle, an iPhone-style status
  bar on iOS devices.

**Exact iOS** (Mac with Xcode and an `ios/` folder, the default there):

- iPhones and iPads render on Flutter's iOS engine: the app's Flutter bundle, built for the
  simulator (skipped when nothing changed), in a generated SwiftUI host app.
- Through the no-boot iOS renderer: pixel identical to a booted simulator, with the real status
  bar.
- Components render at their declared or measured size.

`--flutter-ios headless` renders iOS devices headless too: faster, and the same on every machine.

## Fonts

Android devices use Roboto. Scripts Roboto lacks (Arabic, Hebrew, CJK, Thai, Devanagari) use a
system font that has the script and Latin: Arial Unicode or Hiragino on macOS, DejaVu Sans,
FreeSans or Noto Sans CJK on Linux. On Debian and Ubuntu:

```
sudo apt install fonts-dejavu-core fonts-noto-cjk
```

## Configuration

```json
{
  "devices": ["iPhone 17 Pro Max", "iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)", "Pixel 10 Pro", "Pixel Tablet"],
  "languages": ["en-US", "de", "ar"],
  "appearances": ["light", "dark"],
  "output_directory": "screenshots",
  "clear_previous_screenshots": true
}
```

| key | flag | default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flutter_root` | `--flutter-root` | see [SDK](#sdk) | Flutter SDK |
| `flutter_ios` | `--flutter-ios` | `exact` | `exact` or `headless` for iPhones and iPads |
| `accept_bezel_license` | `--accept-bezel-license` | `false` | Apple's bezel license, for iPhone and iPad frames |

`devices`, `languages`, `appearances`, `font_scales`, `previews`, `screens`, `full_length`,
`delay`, `system_ui`, `frame`, `layout`, `output_directory`, `clear_previous_screenshots`, `html`
and `parallel` work as on [[Android]]:

- `screens`: per-preview devices, languages, appearances, font scales, delay, full length, skip.
- `full_length`: a screen grows until its main scrollable shows everything (on iPhones and iPads
  up to 8192 pixels, Metal's limit).
- `"frame": "plain"`: full screens in their device, in `<output>-framed/`: Android Studio's device
  art for Android devices, Apple's bezels for iPhones and iPads (on a Mac).
- `"layout": "fastlane"`: Android devices in `<language>/images/<type>Screenshots/`.

A layout overflow is a warning, not a failure: the screenshot shows Flutter's overflow stripes.

## Output

```
<output_directory>/<language>/<device>-<preview>[-light|-dark].png
<output_directory>/screenshots.html
<output_directory>/swiftshot-report.json
```

Screenshots are byte identical between runs.

## Speed

`Example/FlutterDemo`, 12 previews in five languages, light and dark:

- 204 screenshots (iPhone and Pixel) headless in about 11 s on an Apple silicon Mac
- the same on a 4-core Linux runner in about 45 s
- exact iOS adds about 1 s per process and 0.8 s per screenshot, in parallel per language and
  device

## Limitations

- Headless, plugins' native code doesn't run.
- Exact iOS needs a Mac with Xcode and an `ios/` folder; elsewhere iOS devices render headless.
- `--mode device` (booted simulators) is the iOS tool's, not Flutter's.
- iPhone and iPad frames need a Mac (Apple's bezels).

# Configuration

`swiftshot init` writes a `swiftshot.json` for the project in the current folder. `--force`
overwrites an existing file.

- iOS: the project or workspace, the app scheme, a watchOS scheme, the languages from the
  project's known regions, and App Store devices installed on the Mac.
- Android: the Android modules from `settings.gradle(.kts)`, the languages the app has
  `values-*/strings*.xml` for, Play devices (Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel Tablet), a
  watch device if a module uses Wear OS, and the `fastlane` layout if the project has a `fastlane`
  folder. Nothing is built.
- Compose Multiplatform: only the modules with `@Preview`s, the languages from
  `composeResources`, and `desktop_devices` / `ios_devices` when the module has those targets.
- Flutter: the languages from the gen-l10n ARB files (`arb-dir` in `l10n.yaml`), iPhone 17 Pro
  Max, iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), Pixel 10 Pro and Pixel Tablet, light and dark.

Swiftshot reads `./swiftshot.json` automatically, or the file given with `--config`. Command-line
flags override the file.

iOS and Android each have their own keys, below. A file with `project`, `workspace` or `scheme`
is an iOS configuration. Unknown keys are an error.

One `swiftshot.json` can serve both: in a Gradle project, and on Linux, the iOS-only keys
(`scheme`, `project`, `mode`, `status_bar`…) are ignored with a note, and `"frame": "appstore"`
gives plain device frames.

- [iOS](#example)
- [Android](#android)
- [Flutter](#flutter)
- [Screenshot testing](#screenshot-testing)

## Example

iOS:

```json
{
  "project": "MyApp.xcodeproj",
  "scheme": "MyApp",
  "devices": ["iPhone 17 Pro Max", "iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)", "Apple Watch Ultra 3 (49mm)"],
  "watch_scheme": "MyWatchApp",
  "ios_versions": ["27.0"],
  "languages": ["en-US", "de-DE", "ja"],
  "appearances": ["light", "dark"],
  "output_directory": "fastlane/screenshots",
  "clear_previous_screenshots": true,
  "screens": [
    { "preview": "Welcome", "appearances": ["light", "dark"] },
    { "preview": "History", "full_length": true },
    { "preview": "Debug*", "skip": true }
  ]
}
```

## Keys

iOS:

| key | default | |
|---|---|---|
| `project` / `workspace` | | Xcode project or workspace |
| `scheme` | | scheme that builds the app |
| `configuration` | `Debug` | must include `#Preview` code, so Debug |
| `app` | | prebuilt simulator `.app` instead of building |
| `derived_data` | `.swiftshot/DerivedData` | |
| `xcodebuild_args` | `[]` | extra `xcodebuild` arguments |
| `devices` | iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) | iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch models |
| `ios_versions` | newest installed | iOS runtimes |
| `watch_scheme` | | scheme of the watchOS app |
| `watch_app` | | prebuilt watchOS simulator `.app` |
| `watchos_versions` | newest installed | watchOS runtimes |
| `languages` | `["en-US"]` | |
| `appearances` | `["light"]` | `light`, `dark` |
| `text_sizes` | `["default"]` | `XS` … `XXXL`, `AX1` … `AX5`, `default` |
| `content_size` | | changes the default text size itself, no file suffix |
| `previews` | all | only previews matching these names or `*` globs |
| `full_length` | `false` | grow screens to their scroll view's whole content (iOS) |
| `output_directory` | `screenshots` | |
| `format` | `png` | `png`, `jpeg` |
| `clear_previous_screenshots` | `false` | |
| `html` | `true` | write `screenshots.html`, and `index.html` in a verify report |
| `status_bar` | `true` | draw the 9:41 status bar |
| `delay` | `0` | seconds to wait before each capture |
| `settle_frames` | `3` | run-loop frames to wait before capture |
| `mode` | `virtual` | `virtual` (no simulator) or `device` (booted reference) |
| `parallel_languages` | `1` | language processes per iOS version at once |
| `timeout` | `600` | seconds before an app launch is killed |
| `download_missing_runtimes` | `false` | download requested runtimes that are missing |
| `allow_unsupported_devices` | `false` | render devices the runtime can't boot (best effort) |
| `shutdown_simulators` | `false` | shut down simulators afterwards |
| `device_set` | | isolated CoreSimulator device set |
| `template_cache` | `~/Library/Caches/swiftshot/templates.noindex` | boot templates for booted modes |
| `frame` | `none` | `plain` or `appstore`, see [[Device frames]] |
| `frame_color` | per model | bezel colour, e.g. `"Deep Blue"` or `{"iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)": "Silver"}` |
| `framefile` | found like frameit | frameit `Framefile.json` |
| `frame_background` | grey | App Store background: `#RRGGBB` or an image |
| `frame_output` | `<output>-framed` | where plain frames go |
| `frame_cache` | `~/Library/Caches/swiftshot/frames` | downloaded bezels |
| `accept_bezel_license` | `false` | accept Apple's Design Resources License without a prompt (CI) |
| `screens` | `[]` | per-screenshot settings, below |

## Per-screenshot settings

Each rule matches previews by name or `*` glob. The first matching rule wins. iOS keys:

| key | |
|---|---|
| `preview` | name or glob |
| `appearances`, `languages`, `devices`, `ios_versions`, `text_sizes` | replace the global list for this preview |
| `full_length` | `true` / `false` |
| `delay` | seconds |
| `skip` | `true` leaves the preview out |
| `frame` | `plain`, `appstore` or `none` for this preview |

On the command line:

```
swiftshot --screen "Welcome: appearances=light,dark" \
          --screen "Stats: languages=de-DE,ja devices=iPad*" \
          --screen "Debug*: skip=true"
```

## Previews

Swiftshot renders each `#Preview` as Xcode would (for `@Preview` see [[Android]]):

- Full screen by default.
- `.sizeThatFitsLayout` and `.fixedLayout(width:height:)` render at their own size.
- `.landscapeLeft` / `.landscapeRight` render in landscape.
- Sheets, alerts and confirmation dialogs presented in the preview are captured fully presented.
- The body can be a SwiftUI view, a `UIViewController` or a `UIView`.

```swift
#Preview("Welcome") { WelcomeView() }
#Preview("Habit row", traits: .sizeThatFitsLayout) { HabitRow(habit: .sample) }
#Preview("New habit") { HabitListView().sheet(isPresented: .constant(true)) { NewHabitView() } }
```

## Output

```
<output_directory>/<language>/<device>-<preview>[-<appearance>][-<text size>][-iOS<version>].png
<output_directory>/screenshots.html
<output_directory>/swiftshot-report.json
```

- `-<appearance>` unless only light is rendered (watch screenshots have none)
- `-<text size>` for non-default text sizes
- `-iOS<version>` when more than one runtime is rendered

The layout is fastlane/deliver's,
so `fastlane deliver` uploads it unchanged.

## Android

```json
{
  "modules": [":app", ":wear"],
  "devices": ["Pixel 10 Pro", "Pixel 9 Pro Fold", "Pixel 9 Pro Fold (folded)", "Pixel Tablet"],
  "watch_devices": ["Wear OS Large Round"],
  "languages": ["en-US", "de-DE", "ja", "ar"],
  "appearances": ["light", "dark"],
  "font_scales": [1, 1.3],
  "output_directory": "fastlane/metadata/android",
  "layout": "fastlane",
  "clear_previous_screenshots": true,
  "screens": [
    { "preview": "Stats", "full_length": true },
    { "preview": "Debug*", "skip": true }
  ]
}
```

| key | default | |
|---|---|---|
| `project_dir` | `.` | the Gradle project, relative to the config file |
| `modules` | every Android module | e.g. `[":app", ":wear"]` |
| `variant` | `debug` | build variant; needs `ui-tooling` on its classpath |
| `gradle_args` | `[]` | extra Gradle arguments |
| `java_home` | | JDK 21+ for Gradle and the renderer, see [[Installation]] |
| `flutter_root` | `FLUTTER_ROOT`, fvm, `flutter` on `PATH` | Flutter SDK, see [[Flutter]] |
| `flutter_ios` | `exact` | Flutter on iPhones and iPads: `exact` (Flutter's iOS engine, Mac with Xcode) or `headless` |
| `devices` | Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel Tablet | phones, foldables, tablets: names, ids or `*` globs (`swiftshot devices`) |
| `watch_devices` | Wear OS Large Round | for Wear OS modules |
| `desktop_devices` | Desktop 1440×900 @2x | Compose Multiplatform desktop window sizes |
| `ios_devices` | iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPad Pro 13-inch (M5) | Compose Multiplatform iOS devices (Mac with Xcode) |
| `ios_versions` | newest installed | iOS runtimes for Compose Multiplatform |
| `platforms` | every target | Compose Multiplatform targets: `android`, `desktop`, `ios` |
| `languages` | `["en-US"]` | BCP 47 tags |
| `appearances` | `["light"]` | `light`, `dark` |
| `font_scales` | `[1]` | 0.5 to 3, e.g. `[1, 1.3, 2]` |
| `previews` | all | only previews matching these names or `*` globs |
| `full_length` | `false` | grow scrolling screens to their whole content |
| `delay` | `0` | seconds to advance the clock before capture |
| `output_directory` | `screenshots` | |
| `layout` | `swiftshot` | `swiftshot` or `fastlane` (below) |
| `clear_previous_screenshots` | `false` | |
| `html` | `true` | write `screenshots.html`, and `index.html` in a verify report |
| `system_ui` | `preview` | status bar and gesture handle: as `showSystemUi` says, `always`, `never` |
| `frame` | `none` | `plain` or `none`, see [[Device frames]] |
| `round_corners` | `black` | outside round watch screens: `black`, `transparent` |
| `android_theme` | the app's theme | window theme; default: the `<application>` theme in the module's manifest, else Material's |
| `parallel` | from cores and memory | renderer processes |
| `screens` | `[]` | per-screenshot settings |

`screens` on Android: `preview`, `appearances`, `languages`, `devices`, `font_scales`,
`full_length`, `delay` and `skip`, as above. `font_scales` takes the place of iOS's `text_sizes`;
there are no `ios_versions` and no per-screen `frame`.

A `preview` pattern with a `.` also matches a preview's fully qualified function
(`com.example.UiKt.Checkout`), which tells apart previews that share a name; one without a `.` matches
names only. A preview's own `device`, `locale`, `uiMode` and `fontScale` normally win over a rule;
`"override_preview": true` (`override_preview=true` on the command line) makes the rule's `devices`,
`languages`, `appearances` and `font_scales` win instead, and its `devices` over `widthDp`/`heightDp`.

```
swiftshot --screen "Stats: languages=de-DE,ja devices=Pixel*" --screen "Debug*: skip=true"
```

A preview's own `device`, `locale`, `uiMode` and `fontScale` win over the matrix, see [[Android]].

### Android output

```
<output_directory>/<language>/<device>-<preview>[-<appearance>][-<font scale>x].png
<output_directory>/screenshots.html
<output_directory>/swiftshot-report.json
```

- `-light` / `-dark` when both are rendered, `-dark` also when only dark is; none on Wear OS or
  when the preview sets `uiMode`
- `-<scale>x` (e.g. `-1.3x`) for a font scale other than 1, or when several are rendered
- `_1`, `_2`… for each `@PreviewParameter` value

With `"layout": "fastlane"` the language folder holds the folders `fastlane supply` uploads:

```
fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/phoneScreenshots/Pixel 10 Pro-Welcome-light.png
fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/tenInchScreenshots/Pixel Tablet-Welcome-light.png
fastlane/metadata/android/en-US/images/wearScreenshots/Wear OS Large Round-Watch list.png
```

Tablets and foldables up to 9" go to `sevenInchScreenshots`, TVs to `tvScreenshots`, desktop
windows to `desktopScreenshots`. For Compose Multiplatform see [[Compose Multiplatform]].

## Flutter

A Flutter project (`pubspec.yaml` on the Flutter SDK) uses the Android keys, with iPhones and iPads
in `devices` too, plus `flutter_root` and `flutter_ios`:

```json
{
  "devices": ["iPhone 17 Pro Max", "iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)", "Pixel 10 Pro", "Pixel Tablet"],
  "languages": ["en-US", "de", "ar"],
  "appearances": ["light", "dark"],
  "flutter_ios": "exact"
}
```

Output: `<output_directory>/<language>/<device>-<preview>[-light|-dark].png`. See [[Flutter]].

## Screenshot testing

Keys for `verify`, `record` and `accept` (all platforms), see [[Screenshot testing]]:

| key | default | |
|---|---|---|
| `baseline_directory` | `screenshots-baseline` | the approved screenshots |
| `report_directory` | `<output_directory>-report` | where `verify` writes what it found |
| `tolerance` | exact | `{"pixels": n, "max_channel_delta": d}`: up to n pixels may differ; a channel may differ by d |

In `screens` rules, also:

| key | |
|---|---|
| `tolerance` | replaces the global `tolerance` for these previews |
| `ignore_regions` | `[[x, y, width, height], …]` in points (iOS) or dp, never compared |

```json
{
  "tolerance": {"max_channel_delta": 1},
  "screens": [{"preview": "Clock*", "ignore_regions": [[0, 0, 120, 44]]}]
}
```

# Command-line

`swiftshot <command> [options]`. `run` is the default command. Run `swiftshot --help` for the same text.

## Platform

One `swiftshot` binary covers both platforms. It renders Android when:

- `--platform android` is given, or
- the project folder (the current one, or `--project-dir`) has `gradlew` and a
  `settings.gradle(.kts)`, no `.xcodeproj` or `.xcworkspace`, no `--project`, `--workspace` or
  `--app`, and no `project`, `workspace` or `scheme` in `swiftshot.json`, or
- it has a `pubspec.yaml` on the Flutter SDK: a [[Flutter]] project.

Otherwise it renders iOS. `--platform ios` forces iOS.

On Linux (and with the Android-only package) `swiftshot` is the Android renderer, with the same
`run`, `list`, `devices` and `init` commands. `--platform android` is accepted. `--platform ios`,
a folder with an Xcode project, and the Mac-only `frame`, `calibrate` and `emit-table` stop with
a message that iOS needs a Mac with Xcode. Compose Multiplatform iOS targets are skipped.

- [iOS](#ios)
- [Android](#android): `swiftshot --platform android --help`

## iOS

```
USAGE
  swiftshot [run|verify|record|accept|list|devices|calibrate|emit-table|init] [options]
  swiftshot frame [<dir>] [frame options]

COMMANDS
  run         Build, render every preview for every device × iOS × language × appearance (default)
  verify      Render as run does (PNG, no frames), then compare with the baseline: exit 0 same,
              1 differences, 2 errors, 64 usage error; the report goes to <output>-report
  record      Render as run does and write the screenshots into the baseline
  accept      Apply a verify report to the baseline without rendering: exit 0 applied (or nothing
              to do), 1 refused (report not from HEAD, push failed), 64 usage or invalid report
  list        Build and print the previews that were discovered
  devices     Show installed iOS runtimes and the geometry used for each device
  calibrate   Boot the given devices once and measure their real safe areas (cached)
  emit-table  Merge calibration.json files into the built-in device table (maintainers)
  init        Write a swiftshot.json for the project here: scheme, watch scheme, languages and
              App Store devices detected (alias auto-setup; --force overwrites an existing one)
  frame       Put existing screenshots (<dir>, default --output) into device frames, like
              `fastlane frameit`. Plain unless --frame appstore.

BUILD
  --project <path> | --workspace <path>   Xcode project or workspace
  --scheme <name>                         Scheme that builds the app
  --configuration <name>                  Default: Debug
  --app <path>                            Use an already-built simulator .app instead of building
  --derived-data <path>                   Default: .swiftshot/DerivedData
  --xcodebuild-arg <arg>                  Extra xcodebuild argument (repeatable)

MATRIX
  --devices "iPhone 17 Pro Max,iPad Pro 13-inch (M5),Apple Watch Ultra 3 (49mm)"
  --ios "26.5,27.1"                       iOS runtime versions (default: newest installed)
  --languages "en-US,de-DE"               Default: en-US
  --appearances "light,dark"              Default: light
  --text-sizes "default,XXXL,AX5"         Dynamic Type sizes to render every preview at: XS S M L XL XXL XXXL
                                          AX1…AX5, or default (the device's own: iOS L, watch L/XL by case
                                          size). Non-default sizes get a "-<size>" file name suffix.
  --full-length                           Grow full-screen previews to their scroll view's whole content
                                          (long lists, forms); per screen: full_length=true
  --previews "Welcome,Onboarding*"        Only these previews (glob); default: all

APPLE WATCH (add watch devices to --devices)
  --watch-scheme <name>                   Scheme of the watchOS app (default: --scheme if only watches are requested)
  --watch-app <path>                      Prebuilt watchOS simulator .app instead of building
  --watchos "27.0"                        watchOS runtime versions (default: newest installed)

OUTPUT
  --output <dir>                          Default: ./screenshots (fastlane/deliver layout: <dir>/<lang>/<device>-<preview>.png)
  --format png|jpeg                       Default: png
  --clear                                 Delete previous screenshots first
  --no-html                               Do not write screenshots.html, or index.html in a verify report
  --no-status-bar                         Leave out the system status bar (9:41, full battery), which is
                                          drawn like on a device by default

DEVICE FRAMES (Apple's Product Bezels, downloaded on first use)
  --frame [plain|appstore|none]           plain: the device with the screenshot in it, transparent, in
                                          <output>-framed/<lang>/<name>_framed.png.
                                          appstore: App Store size with background and localized title
                                          (title.strings / Framefile.json), as <lang>/<name>_framed.png
                                          next to the original, which fastlane deliver uploads instead.
  --frame-color "Deep Blue,iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)=Silver"
                                          Bezel colour, for all devices or per device (default per model)
  --framefile <path>                      frameit Framefile.json (default: found like frameit does)
  --frame-background <#RRGGBB|image>      App Store background (default: light or dark grey by appearance)
  --frame-output <dir>                    Where plain frames go (default <output>-framed)
  --frame-cache <dir>                     Bezel cache (default ~/Library/Caches/swiftshot/frames)
  --accept-bezel-license                  Accept Apple's Design Resources License without the prompt (CI)

RENDERING
  --mode virtual|device                   virtual (default): every device rendered without booting a simulator.
                                          device: a booted simulator per device, framebuffer capture (the
                                          reference virtual is checked against).
  --content-size <size>                   Change the default text size itself (no file name suffix)
  --delay <seconds>                       Extra settle time before each capture (async images, animations)
  --settle-frames <n>                     Run-loop frames to wait before capture (default 3)
  --parallel-languages <n>                Run n language processes concurrently per iOS version (clones)
  --allow-unsupported-devices             Also render devices a runtime can't boot, on another host of the
                                          same runtime (best effort; skipped by default)
  --download-missing-runtimes             Download requested iOS runtimes that are not installed
  --shutdown                              Shut simulators down afterwards (default: keep warm)
  --timeout <seconds>                     Kill an app launch that takes longer (default 600)

PER SCREENSHOT
  --screen "<preview>: key=v1,v2 key=v"     Override settings for previews matching <preview> (glob), repeatable.
                                          keys: appearances, languages, devices, ios, text_sizes, full_length,
                                          delay, skip, frame
                                          e.g. --screen "Welcome: appearances=light,dark languages=en-US"
                                          (or a "screens" array in the JSON config; first match wins)

BASELINE (verify, record; PNG only, no frames)
  --baseline-directory <dir>              Default: screenshots-baseline
  --report-directory <dir>                Default: <output>-report
  (swiftshot.json: "tolerance": {"pixels": n, "max_channel_delta": d}, default exact, or 1 channel
   step with --mode device; per screen also "tolerance" and "ignore_regions": [[x, y, w, h]] in points)

ACCEPT
  --from <dir|zip|url>                    A verify report directory, a zip of one, or an http(s) URL of
                                          the zip (repeatable; SWIFTSHOT_ARTIFACT_TOKEN is sent as the
                                          host's auth header, over https only, to that host only)
  --only "<id>,<id>"                      Only these screenshot ids (repeatable)
  --push                                  Commit the baseline ("Update screenshot baseline (…)") and git push
  --author "Name <email>"                 Commit author (default: swiftshot <swiftshot@users.noreply.github.com>)
  --branch <name>                         With --push: push HEAD to this branch (default: the upstream, or
                                          the CI's branch when HEAD is detached)

CI
  --device-set <dir>                      Use an isolated CoreSimulator device set (simctl --set); created
                                          from scratch, never touches the machine's own simulators
  --template-cache <dir>                  Where per-runtime boot templates live (default ~/Library/Caches/
                                          swiftshot/templates.noindex). Cache it between CI jobs and even the
                                          first boot is skipped.
  --no-templates                          Boot every new simulator from scratch (~35 s each, slow in parallel)
  --boot                                  Render previews in booted simulators. The default renders iOS and
                                          watchOS previews without any simulator: the app runs directly on the
                                          Mac against the runtime (swiftshot-simhost provides Metal/IOSurface).
                                          --mode device always uses booted simulators.

  --config <file>                         JSON config (default ./swiftshot.json if present)
  --json                                  list, devices, verify: print one JSON document to stdout (logs go to
                                          stderr); verify prints its result.json
  --verbose
```

Exit code: 0 when every screenshot was rendered, non-zero otherwise. Errors are listed at the end of the run and in `swiftshot-report.json`.
`verify` exits 0 (same), 1 (differences), 2 (errors) or 64 (usage error); `accept` 0, 1 (refused), 2 (interrupted) or 64. How to use them: [[Screenshot testing]]; the files: [[Baseline format]].
`--json` (outside `list`, `devices` and `verify`), `--from`, `--only`, `--push`, `--author` and `--branch` (outside `accept`), and `--format` and `--frame` on `verify` and `record` are usage errors, 64. Other flags are ignored by a command that doesn't use them. An unknown flag exits 64 on `verify`, `record` and `accept`, and 1 on the other commands.

## Android

```
USAGE
  swiftshot [run|verify|record|accept|list|devices|init] [options]

COMMANDS
  run       Build, render every preview for every device × language × appearance (default)
  verify    Render as run does, then compare with the baseline: exit 0 same, 1 differences,
            2 errors, 64 usage error; the report goes to <output>-report
  record    Render as run does and write the screenshots into the baseline
  accept    Apply a verify report to the baseline without rendering: exit 0 applied (or nothing
            to do), 1 refused (report not from HEAD, push failed), 64 usage or invalid report
  list      Build and print the previews that were found
  devices   List the devices and their screens
  init      Write a swiftshot.json for the project here: modules, languages and Play devices
            detected; with Paparazzi or Roborazzi, the devices of their tests and a
            swiftshot-migration.md report (alias auto-setup; --force overwrites an existing one)

PROJECT
  --project-dir <path>                  Gradle project (default: .)
  --platform android                    Accepted as on the Mac (iOS projects need the Mac tool)
  --modules ":app,:wear"                Modules to render (default: every Android module with previews)
  --variant <name>                      Build variant (default: debug)
  --gradle-arg <arg>                    Extra Gradle argument (repeatable)
  --java-home <path>                    JDK 21+ for the renderer (default: JAVA_HOME, then Android Studio's)
  --flutter-root <path>                 Flutter SDK for Flutter projects (default: FLUTTER_ROOT, fvm, then flutter on PATH)
  --flutter-ios exact|headless          Flutter on iPhones and iPads: Flutter's iOS engine on a Mac with Xcode
                                        (exact, the default) or the headless renderer (faster, any OS)

MATRIX
  --devices "Pixel 10 Pro,Pixel 9 Pro Fold,Pixel Tablet"   Phones, foldables, tablets (default: Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel Tablet)
  --watch-devices "Wear OS Large Round"                    For Wear OS modules (default: Wear OS Large Round)
  --desktop-devices "Desktop 1440×900 @2x"                 Window sizes for Compose Multiplatform desktop
  --ios-devices "iPhone 17 Pro Max,iPad Pro 13-inch (M5)" Compose Multiplatform iOS devices (macOS)
  --ios "27.0"                          iOS runtimes for Compose Multiplatform (default: newest installed)
  --platforms android,desktop,ios       Compose Multiplatform targets to render (default: all the project has)
  --languages "en-US,de-DE"             Default: en-US
  --appearances "light,dark"            Default: light
  --font-scales "1,1.3,2"               Default: 1
  --previews "Welcome,Stats*"           Only previews matching these names or * globs
  --screen "<preview>: key=value …"     Per-screenshot settings (repeatable), e.g.
                                        --screen "Stats: languages=de-DE devices=Pixel*"

OUTPUT
  --output <dir>                        Default: screenshots
  --layout swiftshot|fastlane           fastlane: <output>/<locale>/images/<type>Screenshots
  --clear                               Delete existing screenshots first
  --no-html                             Do not write screenshots.html, or index.html in a verify report
  --full-length                         Grow scrolling screens to their whole content
  --delay <seconds>                     Advance the clock before capture (animations)
  --system-ui preview|always|never      Status and navigation bars (default: as the preview says)
  --frame plain|none                    Put each screenshot in its device (Android Studio's device art)
  --round-corners black|transparent     Outside round watch screens (default: black, as Play requires)
  --parallel <n>                        Renderer processes (default: from cores and memory)

BASELINE (verify, record; PNG only, no frames)
  --baseline-directory <dir>            Default: screenshots-baseline
  --report-directory <dir>              Default: <output>-report

ACCEPT
  --from <dir|zip|url>                  A verify report directory, a zip of one, or an http(s) URL of the zip
                                        (repeatable; SWIFTSHOT_ARTIFACT_TOKEN is sent as the host's
                                        auth header, over https only, to that host only)
  --only "<id>,<id>"                    Only these screenshot ids (repeatable)
  --push                                Commit the baseline ("Update screenshot baseline (…)") and git push
  --author "Name <email>"               Commit author (default: swiftshot <swiftshot@users.noreply.github.com>)
  --branch <name>                       With --push: push HEAD to this branch (default: the upstream, or
                                        the CI's branch when HEAD is detached)

  --config <file>                       Default: ./swiftshot.json
  --json                                list, devices, verify: print one JSON document to stdout (logs go
                                        to stderr); verify prints its result.json
  -v, --verbose
```

The same exit codes as on iOS, and the same flags are usage errors (64) on `verify`, `record` and `accept`; on the other commands they exit 1. `verify`, `record` and `accept` as above, see [[Screenshot testing]]. `swiftshot devices` lists every device with its size in px and dp
and density; `--devices` takes these names, ids (`pixel_9`) or `*` globs. Compose Multiplatform
flags: [[Compose Multiplatform]]. In a Flutter project `--devices` also takes iPhones and iPads,
see [[Flutter]].

## JSON output

`--json` works with `list`, `devices` and `verify`, on every platform. Stdout holds one JSON
document and nothing else; logs, build output and warnings go to stderr. The document has sorted
keys, indented like the files in [[Baseline format]] (the examples are shortened). On any other command `--json` is a
usage error.

`list --json`: the previews in the order the text lists them.

```json
{"previews": [{"name": "Welcome"}, {"name": "Settings"}]}
```

`devices --json`: `width` and `height` are in points on iOS and dp on Android (rounded to 0.01),
`scale` is pixels per point or dp, `platform` is `ios`, `watchos` or `android`.

```json
{"devices": [{"name": "iPhone 17 Pro", "platform": "ios", "width": 402, "height": 874, "scale": 3}],
 "runtimes": ["26.5", "27.0"]}
```

`runtimes` (the installed iOS runtimes) is only in the iOS tool's output. The iOS tool lists the
devices named by `--devices`, the config or the defaults (iPhone 17 Pro Max, iPad Pro 13-inch (M5));
a name it doesn't know exits 1 with `Unknown device`. The Android tool lists
Android Studio's devices, and the iPhones and iPads of [[Flutter]] projects as `ios`.

`verify --json`: stdout is the `result.json` this run wrote, byte for byte ([[Baseline format]]).
Exit codes are the same as without `--json`. When the run ends without a `result.json`
(for example a usage error, 64), stdout stays empty.

```
swiftshot verify --json > result.json
```

# Screenshot-testing

Swiftshot can check that your screens still look the way they did. It keeps a **baseline**: a
folder of approved screenshots in your repository. Every run is compared with it, pixel by pixel.

Works for iOS, Android, Compose Multiplatform and Flutter, with the same commands.

## Three commands

```
swiftshot record                       # render and save the screenshots as the baseline (local use)
swiftshot verify                       # render and compare with the baseline
swiftshot accept --from <report>       # take the changes verify found into the baseline
```

`record` and `verify` take the same options as `swiftshot run` (devices, languages, `--previews`…).
`accept` renders nothing and takes its own: `--from`, `--only`, `--push`, `--author` (see
[[Command line]]).

Baselines are recorded and accepted on CI, so the results are always the same. The flow:

1. **Verify** on CI after every change. It renders, compares and prints what changed:
   ```
   changed  en-US/iPhone 17 Pro-Welcome  (5320 pixels)
   ! Verify failed: 9 unchanged, 1 changed, 0 added, 0 removed, 0 errors → screenshots-report
   ```
   For each changed screenshot, `screenshots-report/images` holds the old one (`baseline`), the
   new one (`new`) and the difference in red (`diff`).
2. A person looks at the result and triggers **accept** on CI (a comment, a manual job or an
   approval, see *On CI* below). `swiftshot accept --from <report> --push` renders nothing; it
   copies the new screenshots into the baseline and commits them. A CI never accepts by itself.
3. The first baseline is made the same way: with no baseline yet, `verify` reports every
   screenshot as added (exit 1), and accept commits them with `baseline.json`.

`accept` only takes a report made on the commit you are on. If something else was committed
since, run `verify` again first.

`swiftshot verify` also runs on your own machine to look at the results. Fonts and rendering can
differ slightly between machines, so a local fingerprint can differ from CI's and `verify` says
so. A baseline recorded locally (`swiftshot record`) is marked `local`; don't commit it.

## On CI

`verify` knows GitHub Actions, GitLab, Bitbucket, Bitrise, Codemagic, CircleCI, Azure Pipelines and
Jenkins. There it comments the result on the pull request, shows it in the CI's own results, and
tells how to accept. Copy the recipe for your CI: [[GitHub Actions|CI-GitHub-Actions]],
[[GitLab|CI-GitLab]], [[Bitbucket|CI-Bitbucket]], [[Bitrise|CI-Bitrise]], [[Codemagic|CI-Codemagic]],
[[CircleCI|CI-CircleCI]], [[Azure Pipelines|CI-Azure-Pipelines]], [[Jenkins|CI-Jenkins]].

`accept --from` takes a folder, a `.zip` or an `https` URL. `--push` commits and pushes to the
pull request's branch (never from a fork); `--branch <name>` names it when the checkout is
detached and the CI doesn't say.

| variable | |
|---|---|
| `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN` | a token for the git host (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket): posts the comment, and pushes to an `https` remote |
| `SWIFTSHOT_ARTIFACT_TOKEN` | a token to download the `--from` URL; sent only to that URL's host |
| `SWIFTSHOT_ARTIFACT_HEADER` | the header to send it in, `Name: value` with `{token}` in the value, e.g. `PRIVATE-TOKEN: {token}`; default per host |
| `SWIFTSHOT_GIT_HOST` | `github`, `gitlab` or `bitbucket`, when the remote's host isn't one of the usual |
| `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_API` | the host's API URL, for a self-hosted one |
| `SWIFTSHOT_COMMIT`, `SWIFTSHOT_BRANCH` | the commit and branch to record, when the CI's own are not the pull request's |
| `SWIFTSHOT_CI` | `false` ignores the CI |

Tokens are never printed and never put in a URL. A failed comment is a warning; the exit code
stays as above.

## Exit codes

| | `verify` | `record` | `accept` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | no differences | recorded | applied, or nothing to apply |
| 1 | differences | | refused (the report isn't from this commit, or `--push` can't push) |
| 2 | errors (a screen failed to render, a file is missing) | errors (screens that failed keep their baseline), or nothing rendered | interrupted |
| 64 | wrong option or config | wrong option or config | wrong option, or not a valid report |

`verify --json` prints the report's `result.json` to stdout and exits with the same codes, see [[Command line]].

## The report

`verify` writes `<output_directory>-report/index.html` (`screenshots-report/index.html` by default).
Open it: it lists what changed, was added or removed, and what failed, and shows each screenshot side by side with its baseline, on a slider, or
as the differences. Tick what you want to keep and it builds the accept command, or on GitHub the
comment to post. `j` and `k` move through the list; `1`, `2`, `3` switch the view. It needs no server
and no network, so a downloaded report works too. `--no-html` leaves it out.

On a pull request, the comment's **Full report** link goes to the CI build, where the report is kept:
download it and open `index.html`. The comment's `Pixels` column is the share of the image that
changed.

## Where files go

```
screenshots/               what this run rendered (output_directory)
screenshots-baseline/      the approved screenshots and baseline.json: commit this
screenshots-report/        what verify found: index.html, result.json, junit.xml, images/
```

Change them with `baseline_directory` and `report_directory` in [[Configuration]], or
`--baseline-directory` and `--report-directory`. A screenshot's id is its path in the folder
without `.png`, e.g. `de-DE/iPhone 17 Pro-Welcome-dark`.

## Small differences

By default every pixel must match (with `--mode device`, a booted simulator, a channel may differ
by 1). To allow more:

```json
{
  "tolerance": {"pixels": 10, "max_channel_delta": 2},
  "screens": [
    {"preview": "Clock*", "ignore_regions": [[0, 0, 120, 44]]}
  ]
}
```

- `pixels`: this many pixels may differ.
- `max_channel_delta`: a pixel counts as different only when a colour channel differs by more
  than this (0–255).
- `ignore_regions`: `[x, y, width, height]` in points (iOS) or dp (Android) that are never
  compared.

Only plain PNG screenshots are compared: no device frames, no JPEG. The file formats are in
[[Baseline format]].

# Agents

How a coding agent adds Swiftshot to a project and keeps its screenshot tests passing. The
previews you already have are the test cases.

## Rules

- **Baselines are recorded and accepted on CI, not on your machine.** Fonts and rendering can
  differ slightly between machines, so a local baseline is marked `local` and may not match CI.
- **A CI never accepts by itself.** A person triggers accept (a comment, a manual job or an
  approval, see the recipes below). Don't run `swiftshot accept` or `swiftshot record` yourself, and
  don't edit the files in `screenshots-baseline`.
- `swiftshot run` and `swiftshot verify` are safe to run locally to see the screens or a diff.

## Install

```
brew install lukasanda/tap/swiftshot
swiftshot --version
```

Other ways (Linux packages, the install script, a CI machine) and the requirements: [[Installation]].
iOS needs an Apple silicon Mac with Xcode; the others need a JDK 21+.

## Set up

In the folder with the `.xcodeproj` or `.xcworkspace` (iOS), `gradlew` (Android, Compose
Multiplatform) or `pubspec.yaml` (Flutter):

```
swiftshot init       # writes swiftshot.json
swiftshot list --json
swiftshot run
```

`init` detects the scheme or modules, languages and devices; it stops if `swiftshot.json` exists
unless `--force` is given. `list` shows which previews were found: if one is missing, see
*Common failures*. `run` writes PNGs and `screenshots.html` to `<output_directory>` (default
`screenshots`; `init` may choose another, e.g. `fastlane/screenshots`). Options: [[Configuration]]
and [[Command line]].

## Previews that render well

Write one preview per screen state worth checking. Load sample data synchronously: images and
animations that are not finished when the screenshot is taken give unstable results (`--delay
<seconds>` waits longer).

| platform | what to write |
|---|---|
| SwiftUI, UIKit | `#Preview` with a SwiftUI view, a `UIViewController` or a `UIView`. Build the Debug configuration: Release builds leave `#Preview` out. `.sizeThatFitsLayout` and `.fixedLayout(width:height:)` render a component at its own size. Sheets and alerts shown by the preview are captured. |
| Compose (Android) | `@Preview` with `showSystemUi = true` for a whole screen, without it for a component. `androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling` must be on the debug classpath (`debugImplementation`). Multipreviews and `@PreviewParameter` work; a preview's own `device`, `locale`, `uiMode` and `fontScale` win over the matrix. See [[Android]]. |
| Compose Multiplatform | `@Preview` (`androidx.compose.ui.tooling.preview.Preview`) in `commonMain`; one run renders the Android, desktop and iOS targets the module has. See [[Compose Multiplatform]]. |
| Flutter | `@Preview` on a public top-level function, static method or widget constructor, in `lib/`. `size` makes a component, without it the preview fills the screen. Private ones are skipped with a warning. See [[Flutter]]. |

## Verify

```
swiftshot verify --json > result.json
```

Stdout is the `result.json` of this run and nothing else; logs go to stderr. Exit 2 can also come
with empty stdout and no `result.json` (a malformed `swiftshot-report.json`, a failed PNG copy; the
error is on stderr): check that stdout is not empty before parsing it. `--json` also works
with `list` and `devices`, see [[Command line]]. The files `verify` writes are in
`<output_directory>-report`: [[Baseline format]] describes every field.

## Read result.json

- `status`: `passed`, `failed` (differences) or `error`. The exit code is 0, 1 or 2.
- `counts`: `unchanged`, `changed`, `added`, `removed`, `errors`.
- `screenshots`: one entry per screenshot; its keys are sorted, so read `id` and `status` by name.
  For every status other than `unchanged`, look at it:
  - `changed`: `reason` and `pixels`, `boxes` (where it differs, `[x, y, w, h]`), and the images
    `baseline`, `new` and `diff`, as paths inside `<output_directory>-report`.
  - `added`, `removed`: the preview has no baseline yet, or its baseline has no preview.
  - `error`: `message` says what failed.
- `errors`: render errors, with the `id` they belong to when known.
- `fingerprintMismatch`: the baseline was made by a different renderer or host; differences may
  come from that.

A change you made on purpose is for a person to accept; a change you didn't is a bug to fix.

The same folder has `index.html`, the report for a person to review. Point them at it instead of
summarising images you can't compare.

## Accept

After a person has looked at the report, accepting happens on CI: for example the comment
`/swiftshot accept` on a pull request (GitHub), or the manual job `swiftshot-accept` (GitLab). The
recipes are listed below. Don't try to accept from your own machine.

The first baseline is made the same way: with no baseline yet, `verify` on CI reports every
screenshot as `added` (exit 1), and a person accepts that report. The accept commits the PNGs and
`baseline.json` with its fingerprints.

## Exit codes

| command | 0 | 1 | 2 | 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run` | every screenshot rendered | a screenshot or the build failed, or a wrong option | | |
| `list`, `devices` | done | failed (the build failed, wrong option) | | |
| `init` | `swiftshot.json` written | failed, or `swiftshot.json` exists and no `--force` | | |
| `verify` | no differences | differences | errors | usage error |
| `record` | recorded | | errors, or nothing rendered | usage error |
| `accept` | applied, or nothing to apply | refused (report is not from this commit, push failed) | interrupted | usage error, or not a valid report |
| `frame`, `calibrate`, `emit-table` (iOS tool) | done | failed | | |

`--json` on any command other than `list`, `devices` and `verify` is a usage error. On the iOS
tool every command exits 64 for such a flag (and for `--from` and the like); the Android tool
exits 1 for it, except `record` and `accept`, which exit 64. Details: [[Command line]],
[[Baseline format]].

## Common failures

| message or symptom | fix |
|---|---|
| no previews found (iOS) | build the Debug configuration; `#Preview` is left out of Release. `swiftshot list` shows what was found. |
| `No @Preview functions found in …` | the module compiled no `@Preview` in that variant; check `--modules` and `--variant`. |
| `… has no androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling on its debug classpath` | add `debugImplementation("androidx.compose.ui:ui-tooling")`. |
| `swiftshot needs a JDK 21 or later` | install a JDK 21+, or set `JAVA_HOME`, `SWIFTSHOT_JAVA_HOME` or `--java-home`. |
| iOS renders instead of Android | pass `--platform android` or `--project-dir` to the Gradle project. |
| a runtime or device is missing (iOS) | `swiftshot devices` lists the devices from `--devices`, the config or the defaults, and the installed runtimes; an unknown name exits 1 with `Unknown device`; `--download-missing-runtimes`, or `--allow-unsupported-devices`. |
| unfinished images or animations | load sample data synchronously, or `--delay <seconds>`. |
| a long list is cut off | `--full-length`, or `"full_length": true` for that screen. |
| `verify` exits 2 | read `errors` and the entries with `status` `error` in `result.json`. |
| `verify` exits 1 with `fingerprintMismatch` | the renderer or host differs from the one that made the baseline; compare on CI. |
| `accept` refuses | the report is from an older commit; run `verify` again. |

More: [[Troubleshooting]].

## CI

[[CI]] lists what each system shows and how a person accepts. The recipes:

- [[GitHub Actions|CI-GitHub-Actions]]
- [[GitLab|CI-GitLab]]
- [[Bitbucket|CI-Bitbucket]]
- [[Bitrise|CI-Bitrise]]
- [[Codemagic|CI-Codemagic]]
- [[CircleCI|CI-CircleCI]]
- [[Azure Pipelines|CI-Azure-Pipelines]]
- [[Jenkins|CI-Jenkins]]

## For your AGENTS.md

````
## Screenshot tests (Swiftshot)
- Previews are the test cases. Add a public preview per screen state, with sample data loaded
  synchronously; iOS builds must be Debug.
- See the screens: `swiftshot run`. Compare: `swiftshot verify --json > result.json`
  (exit 0 same, 1 differences, 2 errors, 64 usage error). With exit 2, stdout can be empty (the
  error is on stderr): don't parse an empty `result.json`.
- Read result.json: `status`, `counts`, and every entry of `screenshots` whose `status` is not
  `unchanged` (`changed` has `diff`, `boxes`, `pixels`; `error` has `message`).
- Fix unintended differences. Never run `swiftshot record` or `swiftshot accept` locally and never
  edit `screenshots-baseline/`: baselines are recorded and accepted on CI, and a person triggers
  the accept. Tell the person which ids changed on purpose.
- Docs: https://github.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/wiki/Agents
````

# CI

| | runner | needs |
|---|---|---|
| iOS | a Mac: the free GitHub-hosted `macos-26` and `xcode-27` runners | Xcode and the runtimes you render |
| Android, Compose Multiplatform (Android, desktop) | any Linux or Mac runner, e.g. the free `ubuntu-latest` | a JDK 21+ and the Android SDK your build uses (preinstalled on GitHub's runners) |

Neither boots a simulator or an emulator, and neither needs a GUI session.

## Screenshot testing on CI

`swiftshot verify` detects these systems from their environment, publishes its results the way
each one shows them and, on a pull request, comments the result. A person accepts the changes in
the way each system offers; nothing is ever accepted on its own. Each page has the recipe.

| | detected by | results | accept |
|---|---|---|---|
| [[GitHub Actions|CI-GitHub-Actions]] | `GITHUB_ACTIONS` | job summary, annotations, `swiftshot` status | comment `/swiftshot accept` |
| [[GitLab|CI-GitLab]] | `GITLAB_CI` | test summary, `expose_as` link | manual job `swiftshot-accept` |
| [[Bitbucket|CI-Bitbucket]] | `BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER` | Tests tab | custom pipeline `swiftshot-accept` |
| [[Bitrise|CI-Bitrise]] | `BITRISE_IO` | Test Reports, `swiftshot-report.zip` | workflow `swiftshot-accept` |
| [[Codemagic|CI-Codemagic]] | `CM_BUILD_ID` | test results | workflow `swiftshot-accept` |
| [[CircleCI|CI-CircleCI]] | `CIRCLECI` | test results, artifacts | approval `accept-screenshots` |
| [[Azure Pipelines|CI-Azure-Pipelines]] | `TF_BUILD` | test results, summary | stage `Accept screenshots` |
| [[Jenkins|CI-Jenkins]] | `JENKINS_URL` | test results, artifacts | stage `Accept screenshots` |

`SWIFTSHOT_CI=false` turns all of this off. The environment variables are in [[Screenshot testing]].

## GitHub Actions

```yaml
jobs:
  ios:
    runs-on: xcode-27
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: LukasAnda/swiftshot@v1.0.0
        with:
          version: 1.0.0
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: ios-screenshots
          path: fastlane/screenshots

  android:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v6
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 21
          cache: gradle
      - uses: LukasAnda/swiftshot@v1.0.0
        with:
          version: 1.0.0
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: android-screenshots
          path: fastlane/metadata/android
```

| input | default | |
|---|---|---|
| `version` | `latest` | swiftshot release to install |
| `args` | | arguments for `swiftshot run`; empty uses `swiftshot.json` |
| `working-directory` | `.` | folder with the project and `swiftshot.json` |

The action runs `install.sh`: on a Linux runner it installs the Android package (Android and
Compose Multiplatform without iOS), on an Apple silicon Mac both platforms. In a Gradle project `swiftshot run` renders Android, see
[[Command line]].

## iOS

Several iOS versions: the runner image ships a few runtimes. Missing ones can be downloaded with
`--download-missing-runtimes` (adds several minutes).

```yaml
      - uses: LukasAnda/swiftshot@v1.0.0
        with:
          args: --ios 26.5,27.1 --download-missing-runtimes
```

Upload to App Store Connect after rendering:

```yaml
      - run: fastlane deliver --skip_binary_upload --skip_metadata --overwrite_screenshots --force
```

## Android

`cache: gradle` in `setup-java` caches Gradle's dependencies and wrapper between runs. Swiftshot's
own cache (unpacked layoutlib, class-data-sharing archives, device art) can be cached too:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/swiftshot/android
          key: swiftshot-android-${{ runner.os }}-1.0.0
```

macOS runners work the same way; there the cache is `~/Library/Caches/swiftshot/android`.

Pass Gradle arguments with `args`, for example a module and a variant:

```yaml
      - uses: LukasAnda/swiftshot@v1.0.0
        with:
          args: --modules :app --variant demoDebug --gradle-arg=--no-daemon
```

Upload to Google Play after rendering with `"layout": "fastlane"`:

```yaml
      - run: fastlane supply --skip_upload_apk --skip_upload_aab --skip_upload_metadata --skip_upload_changelogs --skip_upload_images
```

## Device frames on CI

iOS: accept Apple's bezel license with a flag, and cache the downloaded bezels between runs:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:
          path: ~/Library/Caches/swiftshot/frames
          key: swiftshot-frames-1
      - uses: LukasAnda/swiftshot@v1.0.0
        with:
          args: --frame appstore --accept-bezel-license
```

Android: `--frame plain` needs no license prompt. The device art is downloaded from AOSP once
into Swiftshot's cache, which the cache step above keeps.

## Other CI

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot run --download-missing-runtimes     # iOS
~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot run                                 # Android, in the folder with gradlew
```

Publish the output folder as a build artifact. The exit code is non-zero if any screenshot failed.

## Visual review tools

Plain PNGs with stable names work with screenshot review services:

```
npx @argos-ci/cli upload fastlane/screenshots   # Argos, needs ARGOS_TOKEN
npx @percy/cli upload fastlane/screenshots      # Percy, needs PERCY_TOKEN
```

## Booted simulators on CI

Only `--mode device` and `--boot` boot simulators. Then:

- `--device-set <dir>` keeps the simulators away from the machine's own.
- `--template-cache <dir>` holds per-runtime boot templates. Cache it between jobs to skip the first boot.
- On small runners simulators take turns to stay within memory. `SWIFTSHOT_SIMULATORS=<n>` overrides how many run at once.

# CI-GitHub-Actions

# GitHub Actions

Verify every pull request, and accept the changes by commenting on it.

## Verify

Save as `.github/workflows/screenshots.yml` (the accept workflow looks up its runs by that name).

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: github-workflow docs/recipes/github/screenshots.yml
# Screenshot tests on every pull request: compares against the committed baseline, comments the
# result on the pull request, posts the "swiftshot" commit status and uploads the report.
# iOS needs a Mac runner (e.g. macos-latest); for Android or Compose use ubuntu-latest and add
# actions/setup-java (Temurin 21) before the swiftshot step.
# Branch protection: require the "swiftshot" status, not the "screenshots / verify" check (the
# accept workflow's push with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow, so that check never reruns).
name: screenshots
on: pull_request

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  statuses: write

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - uses: LukasAnda/swiftshot@v1.0.0
        with:
          command: verify
        env:
          SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

The action runs `swiftshot verify`, comments the result on the pull request, posts a `swiftshot`
commit status, writes the summary and the annotations to the run, and uploads the report as the
artifact `swiftshot-report`: download it and open `index.html`. The comment's **Full report** link
goes to the run. Android and Compose: use `ubuntu-latest` and `actions/setup-java`.

## Accept

Save as `.github/workflows/screenshots-accept.yml` on the default branch: `issue_comment`
workflows run from there.

