```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: github-workflow docs/recipes/github/screenshots-accept.yml
# Comment "/swiftshot accept" on a pull request to commit its new screenshots to the baseline.
# Only people with write access can; pull requests from forks are refused.
#   /swiftshot accept                 accepts every difference of the latest run
#   /swiftshot accept <commit>        the same, but only if <commit> is the pull request's head
#   /swiftshot accept <commit>        accepts only these, one id per line (the commit may be left out)
#   en-US/Pixel 9-Home
#   en-US/Pixel 9-Settings
# The report's index.html writes the commit (the one it was rendered from, 7 to 64 hex digits, a
# prefix is enough) so that a comment made from an old report is refused, not applied to a newer
# push. After the command the first line holds nothing else: anything that isn't a commit is refused.
# Save this file on the default branch (issue_comment workflows run from there) and keep the
# runner and setup steps the same as in screenshots.yml, which must be saved under that file name
# (this workflow looks up its runs by it). The verify at the end posts the "swiftshot" status on
# the new head; it does not update the pull request comment (an issue_comment event has no pull
# request number for it).
name: screenshots-accept
on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  statuses: write
  actions: read

concurrency:
  group: swiftshot-accept-${{ github.event.issue.number }}

jobs:
  accept:
    if: github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/swiftshot accept')
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check the commenter and find the report
        id: prepare
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.event.comment.user.login }}
          COMMENT: ${{ github.event.comment.body }}
        run: |
          reply() { gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR/comments" -f body="$1" > /dev/null; }
          refuse() { reply "$1"; echo "proceed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0; }

          first=$(printf '%s\n' "$COMMENT" | head -n 1 | tr -d '\r')
          case "$first" in
            "/swiftshot accept" | "/swiftshot accept "*) ;;
            *) echo "proceed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0 ;;
          esac

          permission=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/collaborators/$ACTOR/permission" --jq .permission 2>/dev/null || echo none)
          case "$permission" in
            admin | maintain | write) ;;
            *) refuse "@$ACTOR only people with write access can accept screenshots." ;;
          esac

          # The first line may end in the commit the report was rendered from. It is only ever compared
          # as text, never run or put in a command, and has to be hex before it is even shown.
          token=$(printf '%s' "${first#"/swiftshot accept"}" | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//')
          if [ -n "$token" ]; then
            case "$token" in
              *[!0-9a-fA-F]*) refuse "Nothing after \`/swiftshot accept\` on its first line may be anything but the commit of the report (7 or more hex digits). Put screenshot ids one per line below it." ;;
            esac
            [ "${#token}" -ge 7 ] && [ "${#token}" -le 64 ] || refuse "The commit after \`/swiftshot accept\` must be 7 to 64 hex digits."
            token=$(printf '%s' "$token" | tr 'A-F' 'a-f')
          fi

          pr=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR")
          sha=$(jq -r .head.sha <<< "$pr")
          [ -z "$token" ] || [[ "$sha" == "$token"* ]] || refuse "That report is out of date: it was rendered from ${token:0:7} and the pull request is now at ${sha:0:7}. Nothing was accepted. Open the report of the latest run and comment again."
          ref=$(jq -r .head.ref <<< "$pr")
          head_repo=$(jq -r '.head.repo.full_name // empty' <<< "$pr")
          [ "$head_repo" = "$REPO" ] || refuse "This pull request comes from a fork, so swiftshot can't push to it. Download the report and run \`swiftshot accept --from <report>\` in the fork."

          run=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/screenshots.yml/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=pull_request&status=completed&per_page=1" --jq '.workflow_runs[0].id // empty')
          [ -n "$run" ] || refuse "No finished screenshots run for ${sha:0:7} yet. Wait for it, or push again."
          url=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$run/artifacts?name=swiftshot-report" --jq '[.artifacts[] | select(.expired == false)][0].archive_download_url // empty')
          [ -n "$url" ] || refuse "The report of the screenshots run for ${sha:0:7} is missing or expired. Push again to render a new one."

          # The ids: one per line after the first (ids contain spaces).
          ids=()
          while IFS= read -r line; do
            line=$(printf '%s' "$line" | tr -d '\r' | sed -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//')
            [ -z "$line" ] || ids+=("$line")
          done < <(printf '%s\n' "$COMMENT" | tail -n +2)
          # Quoted for the action, which reads its args like a shell line. --only splits on commas.
          args=$(printf '%q ' --push --branch "$ref")
          for id in "${ids[@]}"; do
            case "$id" in *,*) refuse "An id can't contain a comma: \`$id\`" ;; esac
            args+=$(printf '%q %q ' --only "$id")
          done

          {
            echo "proceed=true"
            echo "url=$url"
            echo "ref=$ref"
            echo "args=$args"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        if: steps.prepare.outputs.proceed == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.ref }}

      # Pushes with the credentials checkout persisted; do not set SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN here.
      - name: Accept
        id: accept
        if: steps.prepare.outputs.proceed == 'true'
        uses: LukasAnda/swiftshot@v1.0.0
        with:
          command: accept
          from: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.url }}
          args: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.args }}
        env:
          SWIFTSHOT_ARTIFACT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: New head
        id: head
        if: steps.prepare.outputs.proceed == 'true'
        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # A push with GITHUB_TOKEN starts no workflow: render once more here, which posts the
      # "swiftshot" status on the new commit. An issue_comment run sees the default branch's commit
      # and name, so the pull request's are given. Differences left after a partial accept fail
      # the status, not this job.
      - name: Verify the new baseline
        if: steps.prepare.outputs.proceed == 'true'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: LukasAnda/swiftshot@v1.0.0
        with:
          command: verify
          report-name: swiftshot-report-accepted
        env:
          SWIFTSHOT_COMMIT: ${{ steps.head.outputs.sha }}
          SWIFTSHOT_BRANCH: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.ref }}

      - name: Thumbs up
        if: steps.accept.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          COMMENT_ID: ${{ github.event.comment.id }}
        run: gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/comments/$COMMENT_ID/reactions" -f content='+1' > /dev/null || echo "::warning::Could not react to the comment"

      - name: Reply with the error
        # Only when checking or accepting failed; a refusal already replied and exited 0.
        if: failure() && (steps.prepare.outcome == 'failure' || steps.accept.outcome == 'failure')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$PR/comments" -f body="Accepting failed, see the log: $RUN_URL" > /dev/null
```

Comment `/swiftshot accept` on the pull request. To take only some changes, list their ids one
per line below the command. The workflow checks that the commenter has write access, that the
pull request is not from a fork and that the report is from the pull request's head, then pushes
the new baseline to its branch and verifies it again.

The report's `index.html` writes the comment for you, always with the commit it was rendered from
on the first line: `/swiftshot accept <commit>`, then the ids one per line when you ticked only some.
If that commit is no longer the pull request's head (someone pushed after the report was made), the
workflow replies that the report is out of date and accepts nothing, so you never accept changes you
have not seen. The commit is 7 to 64 hex digits and a prefix of the head is enough. A bare
`/swiftshot accept`, as the pull request comment suggests, still accepts the latest run's changes.
Nothing else may follow the command on its first line: the ids go on the lines below, and anything
on the first line that is not a commit is refused. The commit is only compared as text; it never
reaches a shell command.

## Comment

`GITHUB_TOKEN` is enough: the `permissions` above give it `pull-requests: write` (the comment)
and `statuses: write` (the status). The accept workflow pushes with the credentials that
`actions/checkout` keeps, so it sets no `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN`. If you push with your own
`SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN` instead (to start workflows on the new commit, use a fine-grained token with
Contents write), set `persist-credentials: false` on the checkout: two credentials make GitHub
refuse the push.

## Notes

- A `pull_request` run is checked out as a merge with the base branch. The recipe checks out the
  pull request's head and `swiftshot` records it, so reports and accepts refer to the same
  commit.
- Pull requests from forks get a read-only token: no comment, and accept refuses them.
- A push with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no workflow, which is why the accept workflow verifies the
  new head itself. In branch protection, require the `swiftshot` status, not the
  `screenshots / verify` check.
- Reports are kept as long as your artifact retention says.
- The action's inputs and the rest of the setup are in [[CI]].

# CI-GitLab

# GitLab CI

Verify every merge request, publish the report, and let a person accept the changes with one click.

## Verify

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: gitlab-ci
stages: [verify, accept]

# iOS needs a Mac runner (add its tags); Android needs a JDK 21+ image.
verify:
  stage: verify
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
  script:
    - curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
    - ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot verify
  artifacts:
    when: always
    expire_in: 14 days
    paths:
      - screenshots-report/
    expose_as: swiftshot report
    reports:
      junit: screenshots-report/junit.xml
```

A changed screenshot fails the job. `junit.xml` fills the merge request's test summary, `expose_as`
links the report in the merge request, and `summary.md` is in the report folder. Download the
artifacts and open `index.html`; the comment's **Full report** link goes to the job.

## Accept

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: gitlab-ci
swiftshot-accept:
  stage: accept
  rules:
    - if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"
      when: manual
      allow_failure: true
  # No needs: verify failed, and a manual job that needs a failed job is not offered.
  needs: []
  # On Linux swiftshot runs on Java: a JDK 21+ image with git, curl and python3 (verify's will do).
  script:
    - curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
    # The runner's origin carries the job token; push with SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN instead.
    - git remote set-url origin "$CI_SERVER_URL/$CI_PROJECT_PATH.git"
    # The artifacts of this pipeline's verify job, fetched with the same token (needs curl and python3).
    # The header comes from stdin, so the token is not on curl's command line.
    - >
      verify_job=$(printf 'PRIVATE-TOKEN: %s\n' "$SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN"
      | curl -fsS --header @- "$CI_API_V4_URL/projects/$CI_PROJECT_ID/pipelines/$CI_PIPELINE_ID/jobs?per_page=100"
      | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(next(j['id'] for j in json.load(sys.stdin) if j['name'] == 'verify'))")
    - export SWIFTSHOT_ARTIFACT_TOKEN="$SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN"
    - ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot accept --from "$CI_API_V4_URL/projects/$CI_PROJECT_ID/jobs/$verify_job/artifacts" --push
```

Run the job from the merge request's pipeline once its verify job has finished. It downloads the
report of that pipeline's verify job through the API (`needs` would hide the job, because verify
failed). It commits the new screenshots to the merge request's source branch, which starts a new
pipeline. To take only some, add `--only "<id>,<id>"`.

## Comment

Set `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN` (CI/CD variable, masked) to a **project access token** with the scopes
`api` (merge request comments) and `write_repository` (push) and the Developer role or higher.
Without it nothing is posted and the push uses the runner's own credentials, which usually
can't push.

## Notes

- A job token can't comment, and can push only if the project allows it (Settings, CI/CD, Job
  token permissions); the access token above is used for the comment, the report download and the
  push.
- Merge request pipelines from a fork run in the fork: accept refuses them.
- With "merged results" pipelines the job renders the merge, not the source branch; use plain
  merge request pipelines for screenshot tests.
- Reports expire with the artifacts (14 days above).
- `accept` pushes the commit with the access token over `https`; self-managed GitLab works the
  same, set `SWIFTSHOT_GIT_HOST=gitlab` if the host isn't recognised.

# CI-Bitbucket

# Bitbucket Pipelines

Verify every pull request, and accept the changes with a custom pipeline you run by hand.

## Verify

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: bitbucket-pipelines
# iOS needs a Mac runner (runs-on: [self.hosted, macos]); Android needs a JDK 21+ image.
image: atlassian/default-image:4

pipelines:
  pull-requests:
    '**':
      - step:
          name: Verify screenshots
          script:
            - curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
            # The pipeline checks out a merge with the destination; the report is for the source commit.
            - export SWIFTSHOT_COMMIT="$BITBUCKET_COMMIT"
            # The pipeline's own remote is a local proxy: name the real one, after the clone, for the comment.
            - git remote set-url origin "https://bitbucket.org/$BITBUCKET_REPO_FULL_NAME.git"
            - ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot verify
          # Runs after a failed script too: keep the report where the accept pipeline finds it.
          after-script:
            - >
              if [ -d screenshots-report ]; then
              python3 -m zipfile -c "swiftshot-report-$BITBUCKET_COMMIT.zip" screenshots-report &&
              printf 'Authorization: Bearer %s\n' "$SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN" |
              curl -fsS -X POST --header @- -F "files=@swiftshot-report-$BITBUCKET_COMMIT.zip"
              "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/$BITBUCKET_REPO_FULL_NAME/downloads"; fi
```

A changed screenshot fails the step (`junit.xml` is copied to `test-results/` for the Tests tab).
The after-script uploads the report to the repository's Downloads as
`swiftshot-report-<commit>.zip`, because Bitbucket has no API for a pipeline's artifacts. Unzip it
and open `index.html`; the comment's **Full report** link goes to the pipeline.

## Accept

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: bitbucket-pipelines
pipelines:
  custom:
    swiftshot-accept:
      - step:
          name: Accept screenshots
          # On Linux swiftshot runs on Java: the image needs JDK 21+ (verify's will do).
          script:
            - curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
            - export SWIFTSHOT_ARTIFACT_TOKEN="$SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN"
            # After the clone, so that the push goes to Bitbucket with the token.
            - git remote set-url origin "https://bitbucket.org/$BITBUCKET_REPO_FULL_NAME.git"
            - >
              ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot accept --push --branch "$BITBUCKET_BRANCH" --from
              "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/$BITBUCKET_REPO_FULL_NAME/downloads/swiftshot-report-$BITBUCKET_COMMIT.zip"
```

Add it to the same `pipelines` as the verify step. Run it from the Pipelines page: "Run
pipeline", the pull request's branch, `swiftshot-accept`. It picks the report of the branch's
latest commit; if the branch moved on, verify again first.

## Comment

Set `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN` (secured repository variable) to a **repository access token** with
the scopes `repository`, `repository:write` (push, Downloads) and `pullrequest` (comments).
Set `SWIFTSHOT_GIT_HOST=bitbucket` if your remote isn't `bitbucket.org`.

## Notes

- A failed step stops a pipeline, so a manual step after verify could never be reached: accept is
  its own custom pipeline.
- Pull request pipelines merge the destination branch into the working tree before they run.
  `BITBUCKET_COMMIT` is the pull request's source commit, so `SWIFTSHOT_COMMIT` is set from it.
  The accept pipeline runs on the branch itself, where `BITBUCKET_COMMIT` is the same commit.
- The reports stay in the repository's Downloads (one per verified commit) until someone deletes
  them; remove old ones with `DELETE /2.0/repositories/<workspace>/<repo>/downloads/<name>`.
- Pull requests from forks don't start pipelines.
- A push starts a new pipeline, which verifies the new baseline.

# CI-Bitrise

# Bitrise

Verify in one workflow, accept in a second one you start by hand.

## Verify

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: bitrise
format_version: "11"

workflows:
  swiftshot-verify:
    steps:
      - git-clone@8:
          inputs:
            - merge_pr: "no"
      - script@1:
          title: swiftshot verify
          inputs:
            - content: |
                #!/usr/bin/env bash
                set -eu
                curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
                ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot verify
      - deploy-to-bitrise-io@2:
          is_always_run: true
```

Start it from a trigger on pull requests. `verify` writes `swiftshot-report.zip` to
`$BITRISE_DEPLOY_DIR` and its test results to the Test Reports tab itself; the deploy step
uploads both, also when verify failed. Unzip the report and open `index.html`; the comment's
**Full report** link goes to the build.

## Accept

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: bitrise
format_version: "11"

workflows:
  swiftshot-accept:
    steps:
      - git-clone@8:
          inputs:
            - merge_pr: "no"
      - script@1:
          title: swiftshot accept
          inputs:
            - content: |
                #!/usr/bin/env bash
                set -eu
                curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
                api="https://api.bitrise.io/v0.1/apps/$BITRISE_APP_SLUG/builds/$SWIFTSHOT_VERIFY_BUILD/artifacts"
                pick() { python3 -c "import json,sys; $1"; }
                # The header comes from stdin, so the token is not on curl's command line.
                get() { printf 'Authorization: %s\n' "$BITRISE_TOKEN" | curl -fsS -H @- "$1"; }
                slug=$(get "$api" |
                  pick "print(next(a['slug'] for a in json.load(sys.stdin)['data'] if a['title'] == 'swiftshot-report.zip'))")
                url=$(get "$api/$slug" | pick "print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['expiring_download_url'])")
                ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot accept --from "$url" --push
```

Start `swiftshot-accept` on the pull request's branch ("Start/Schedule a build") with the
environment variable `SWIFTSHOT_VERIFY_BUILD` set to the slug of the verify build (the last part
of its URL). The download link is signed and short-lived, so no token goes with it.

## Comment

Set these as secrets:

- `BITRISE_TOKEN`: a Bitrise personal access token, to list the verify build's artifacts.
- `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN`: a token for your git host. GitHub: fine-grained, Contents and Pull
  requests write. GitLab: `api` and `write_repository`. Bitbucket: repository access token with
  `repository:write` and `pullrequest`. It posts the comment and, over `https`, pushes.

To push over SSH instead, give the app an SSH key with write access: Bitrise's default
deploy key is usually read-only. Without a push token the SSH key is what accept uses.

## Notes

- Bitrise builds the merge of the pull request by default; `merge_pr: "no"` checks out its head
  so the report and the accept refer to the same commit.
- Artifacts are kept for 365 days; a signed link lasts about ten minutes, so the accept build
  fetches it when it runs.
- Accept won't run for pull requests from forks.

# CI-Codemagic

# Codemagic

Verify in one workflow, accept in a second one you start by hand.

## Verify

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: codemagic
workflows:
  swiftshot-verify:
    name: swiftshot verify
    instance_type: mac_mini_m2
    triggering:
      events:
        - pull_request
      branch_patterns:
        - pattern: '*'
          include: true
          source: true
    scripts:
      - name: swiftshot verify
        script: |
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
          ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot verify && status=0 || status=$?
          # Zip also after differences, then fail the build with verify's exit code.
          [ ! -d screenshots-report ] || zip -qr swiftshot-report.zip screenshots-report
          exit $status
        test_report: screenshots-report/junit.xml
    artifacts:
      - swiftshot-report.zip
      - screenshots-report/**
```

`test_report` shows the differences in the build's test results. The script zips the report before
it exits with verify's exit code, so a build with differences fails and still has the zip.
The workflow runs on pull request branches. Unzip the report and open `index.html`; Codemagic gives
no build URL, so the comment has no **Full report** link.

## Accept

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: codemagic
workflows:
  swiftshot-accept:
    name: swiftshot accept
    instance_type: mac_mini_m2
    scripts:
      - name: swiftshot accept
        script: |
          set -eu
          curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
          pick() { python3 -c "import json,sys; $1"; }
          # The headers come from stdin, so the token is not on curl's command line.
          api() { printf 'x-auth-token: %s\nContent-Type: application/json\n' "$CODEMAGIC_TOKEN" | curl -fsS -H @- "$@"; }
          artifact=$(api "https://api.codemagic.io/builds/$SWIFTSHOT_VERIFY_BUILD" |
            pick "print(next(a['url'] for a in json.load(sys.stdin)['build']['artefacts'] if a['url'].endswith('/swiftshot-report.zip')))")
          url=$(api -d "{\"expiresAt\": $(( $(date +%s) + 600 ))}" "$artifact/public-url" |
            pick "print(json.load(sys.stdin)['url'])")
          ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot accept --from "$url" --push
```

This workflow has no triggers, so it only starts by hand: "Start new build" on the pull request's
branch with the workflow `swiftshot-accept` and the variable `SWIFTSHOT_VERIFY_BUILD` set to the
verify build's id (the last part of its URL), or the same through the builds API.

## Comment

Set these as secure variables:

- `CODEMAGIC_TOKEN`: a Codemagic API token, to find the verify build's artifact.
- `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN`: a token for your git host, which comments and pushes over `https`.
  GitHub: fine-grained, Contents and Pull requests write. GitLab: `api` and `write_repository`.
  Bitbucket: repository access token with `repository:write` and `pullrequest`.

Codemagic documents pushing only over `https` with a token, so there is no SSH variant.

## Notes

- The link from the public-url call is short-lived and open to anyone who has it, so it expires in
  ten minutes and is passed to `accept` without a token.
- Codemagic's docs don't say whether artifacts and `test_report` are kept for a failed build; check
  that the zip appears on your first build with a difference.
- Codemagic describes `CM_COMMIT` as the pull request's source commit, which is what verify
  records.
- The artifact list of a build is read from the builds API (`build.artefacts`, with that
  spelling); check it against your account if the lookup fails.

# CI-CircleCI

# CircleCI

Verify on every push, then approve a job in the same workflow to accept.

## Verify

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: circleciconfig
version: 2.1

jobs:
  verify:
    # iOS: a Mac executor with an Xcode version CircleCI offers.
    # Android: a Linux image with JDK 21+ instead.
    macos:
      xcode: "26.0.0"
    steps:
      - checkout
      - run:
          name: Install swiftshot
          command: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
      - run:
          name: Verify
          command: ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot verify
      # The steps below run after a failed verify too.
      - store_test_results:
          when: always
          path: screenshots-report
      - store_artifacts:
          when: always
          path: screenshots-report
          destination: swiftshot-report
      - persist_to_workspace:
          when: always
          root: .
          paths:
            - screenshots-report
```

A changed screenshot fails the job. `store_test_results` reads `junit.xml` from the report folder;
`store_artifacts` keeps the report for the job's Artifacts tab, where `index.html` opens it; the
comment's **Full report** link goes to the job.

## Accept

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: circleciconfig
version: 2.1

jobs:
  accept:
    docker:
      - image: cimg/openjdk:21.0
    steps:
      - checkout
      - attach_workspace:
          at: .
      # A read-write deploy key added under Project Settings, SSH Keys.
      - add_ssh_keys:
          fingerprints:
            - "SHA256:replace-with-the-fingerprint"
      - run:
          name: Install swiftshot
          command: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
      - run:
          name: Accept
          command: |
            ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot accept --from screenshots-report --push

workflows:
  screenshots:
    jobs:
      - verify
      - accept-screenshots:
          type: approval
          requires:
            - verify:
                - failed
      - accept:
          requires:
            - accept-screenshots
```

Both snippets are one `config.yml`. Whoever has push access
approves `accept-screenshots` in the workflow view; `accept` then pushes the new baseline.

## Comment

Set `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN` as a project environment variable to post the pull request comment
(GitHub: fine-grained, Pull requests write; GitLab: `api`; Bitbucket: `pullrequest`). It is not
used for the push.

## Notes

- CircleCI's checkout key is read-only, hence `add_ssh_keys`. The push stays on ssh: `checkout`
  rewrites `https://github.com` to ssh globally, so a token can't push. The key must be added in the
  project settings; an environment variable can't hold it.
- The approval only appears when verify failed, so a clean run never waits for a person
  (`requires` with a status is CircleCI's "flexible requires"). The workspace and the approval both
  live in the workflow, so verify and accept are one run. Workspaces are kept for 15 days; an
  approval can be given for 90.
- CircleCI's docs don't say that a failed job's workspace can be attached by a later job. If
  `attach_workspace` finds nothing in your first failing run, download the `swiftshot-report`
  artifact instead.
- A fork's pull request has no secrets and the key isn't available: accept refuses forks.
- `store_artifacts` links need a CircleCI login on private projects.

# CI-Azure-Pipelines

# Azure Pipelines

Verify pull requests, then approve a stage of the same run to accept.

## Verify

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: azure-pipelines
trigger: none
pr:
  - main

stages:
  - stage: Verify
    jobs:
      - job: verify
        pool:
          vmImage: macos-latest
        steps:
          - checkout: self
          - script: |
              curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
              ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot verify
            displayName: Verify
          - task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
            condition: succeededOrFailed()
            inputs:
              targetPath: screenshots-report
              artifact: swiftshot-report
```

`verify` publishes the JUnit results and the summary to the run itself. Add a
`PublishTestResults@2` task for `screenshots-report/junit.xml` only if you want it in your own
test run. For Azure Repos, use a branch policy (build validation) instead of `pr:`. Download the
`swiftshot-report` artifact and open `index.html`; the comment's **Full report** link goes to the run.

## Accept

```yaml
# swiftshot-recipe: azure-pipelines
stages:
  - stage: Accept
    displayName: Accept screenshots
    dependsOn: Verify
    # Only when verify found differences; a clean pull request never waits for a person.
    condition: and(eq(dependencies.Verify.result, 'Failed'), eq(variables['Build.Reason'], 'PullRequest'))
    jobs:
      - job: wait
        pool: server
        timeoutInMinutes: "4320"
        steps:
          - task: ManualValidation@0
            timeoutInMinutes: 1440
            inputs:
              notifyUsers: ''
              instructions: Accept the new screenshots?
              onTimeout: reject
      - job: accept
        dependsOn: wait
        pool:
          vmImage: macos-latest
        steps:
          - checkout: self
            persistCredentials: "true"
            fetchDepth: "0"
          - task: DownloadPipelineArtifact@2
            inputs:
              artifactName: swiftshot-report
              targetPath: $(Pipeline.Workspace)/swiftshot-report
          - script: |
              curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
              branch="${SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_SOURCEBRANCH#refs/heads/}"
              git fetch origin "$branch"
              git checkout -B "$branch" "origin/$branch"
              ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot accept --from "$(Pipeline.Workspace)/swiftshot-report" --push
            displayName: Accept
```

Both snippets are stages of one file; the accept stage appears only when verify failed. Users with
the **Queue builds** permission approve the `Accept screenshots` stage in the run, and the stage
rejects itself after a day.

## Comment

- **Azure Repos**: no token. Give `<project> Build Service (<organization>)` the permissions
  Contribute, Create branch and Read on the repository (Project settings, Repos, Security);
  `persistCredentials: true` lets `accept` push with it. Azure Repos has no comment support:
  the run's summary and test results carry the result.
- **GitHub or Bitbucket repository**: set `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN` as a secret variable and pass it
  to the verify and accept scripts with `env: SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN: $(SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN)`;
  secrets aren't exposed to scripts otherwise. Use `persistCredentials: false` there. GitHub:
  fine-grained token with Contents and Pull requests write. Bitbucket: repository access token
  with `repository:write` and `pullrequest`.

## Notes

- Azure builds the merge of the pull request; `verify` records the pull request's source commit
  (`System.PullRequest.SourceCommitId`), and the accept job checks out the source branch so both
  refer to the same commit. If the branch moved on, accept refuses and says to verify again.
- The pipeline artifact is read in the accept job with `DownloadPipelineArtifact@2`; no token goes
  to the REST API.
- The server job that holds the approval can't run scripts, hence the second job.
- Fork pull requests: accept refuses them.

# CI-Jenkins

# Jenkins

Verify pull requests in a multibranch pipeline, then approve an `input` stage to accept.

Checked against the docs only: Jenkins has no schema, so the Jenkinsfile below is checked for
balanced braces, not run.

## Verify

```groovy
// swiftshot-recipe: jenkins
// In a Jenkinsfile of the form: pipeline { agent none; stages { <the stages below> } }
stage('Verify') {
  agent { label 'mac' }
  steps {
    sh 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh'
    // Differences fail the stage and mark the build unstable; the accept stage still follows.
    catchError(buildResult: 'UNSTABLE', stageResult: 'FAILURE') {
      sh '~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot verify'
    }
  }
  post {
    always {
      junit 'screenshots-report/junit.xml'
      archiveArtifacts artifacts: 'screenshots-report/**'
      stash name: 'swiftshot-report', includes: 'screenshots-report/**'
    }
  }
}
```

`archiveArtifacts` keeps the report with the build, which the comment's **Full report** link goes to.
Download it and open `index.html`: Jenkins's default Content-Security-Policy stops the page's script
when it is viewed in place.

## Accept

```groovy
// swiftshot-recipe: jenkins
stage('Accept screenshots') {
  options {
    timeout(time: 1, unit: 'DAYS')
  }
  when {
    beforeInput true
    allOf {
      changeRequest()
      expression { !env.CHANGE_FORK }
      // Only when verify found differences; a clean pull request never waits for a person.
      expression { currentBuild.currentResult == 'UNSTABLE' }
    }
  }
  input {
    message 'Accept the new screenshots?'
    ok 'Accept'
  }
  agent { label 'git' }
  steps {
    checkout scm
    unstash 'swiftshot-report'
    withCredentials([string(credentialsId: 'swiftshot-host-token', variable: 'SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN')]) {
      sh '''
        curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LukasAnda/swiftshot/main/install.sh | SWIFTSHOT_VERSION=1.0.0 sh
        git checkout -B "$CHANGE_BRANCH"
        ~/.swiftshot/bin/swiftshot accept --from screenshots-report --push
      '''
    }
  }
}
```

Both stages go into the same `stages`, one after the other. Anyone who may use the build
(add `submitter 'alice,bob'` to limit it) presses Accept on the stage; `stash` carries the report
to it. The stage only appears when the build is unstable (the differences), and gives up after a
day. On a Linux agent swiftshot runs on Java: the `git` agent needs JDK 21+.

## Comment

Add a *Secret text* credential `swiftshot-host-token` with a token for your git host. It posts the
comment and pushes over `https`. GitHub: fine-grained, Contents and Pull requests write. GitLab:
`api` and `write_repository`. Bitbucket: repository access token with `repository:write` and
`pullrequest`. Set `SWIFTSHOT_GIT_HOST` (github, gitlab, bitbucket) if the remote's host isn't
`github.com`, `gitlab.com` or `bitbucket.org`.

## Notes

- In the multibranch project's branch source, set the pull request discovery strategy to
  **The current pull request revision**. With the merge strategy `GIT_COMMIT` is a merge
  commit and the report would not match the branch; in that case set `SWIFTSHOT_COMMIT` to
  the pull request's head commit yourself.
- `stash` lasts for the run, so accept must happen in the same build. The `input` stage uses
  no executor while it waits (`agent none` at the top).
- Differences fail the Verify stage and mark the build unstable (yellow, not green); the
  `catchError` keeps the pipeline going so the accept stage can follow.
- Pull requests from forks: accept refuses them (`CHANGE_FORK`).

# Baseline-format

The files `verify`, `record` and `accept` read and write. Both implementations (the Swift binary
and the JVM CLI) follow this page exactly and are tested against the fixtures in
`Shared/testdata/baseline` (regenerate inputs with `python3 -I Shared/testdata/baseline/make.py`).

## Layout

```
<baseline_directory>/                 default screenshots-baseline
  <id>.png
  baseline.json
<output_directory>/                   what the run wrote
  <id>.png
  swiftshot-report.json
<report_directory>/                   default <output_directory>-report
  result.json
  junit.xml
  summary.md
  index.html                          the same result for people (see index.html); not with --no-html
  manifest.json
  timings.json                        {"compareSeconds": 0.25}: how long the comparison took
  images/baseline/<id>.png            changed and removed
  images/new/<id>.png                 changed and added
  images/diff/<id>.png                changed
```

`timings.json`: the seconds `verify` spent comparing and writing the report, to the millisecond. It
differs between runs, so it is kept out of `result.json` (which stays byte-identical). With
`totalSeconds` of `swiftshot-report.json` (the run) it gives the comparison's overhead.

Relative `baseline_directory` and `report_directory` resolve against the current directory on the
Mac (iOS; flags and swiftshot.json alike, as `output_directory`). On the JVM side a flag resolves
against the current directory (Flutter projects: `--project-dir`) and a swiftshot.json value against
the folder of that file.

**Screenshot id**: the PNG's path relative to the output directory, `/`-separated, without `.png`,
e.g. `de-DE/iPhone 17 Pro-Welcome-dark`. File names are the ones `run` writes today (appearance,
text size, font scale, iOS runtime parts included).

Examples below are abbreviated and not in the sorted key order the files use.

## Exit codes

| code | |
|---|---|
| 0 | no differences |
| 1 | differences (changed, added or removed) |
| 2 | errors, with or without differences |
| 64 | usage error |

`verify --json` prints `result.json` to stdout, byte for byte, and exits the same. A run that ends without a `result.json` (64, or an error before the comparison finished) prints nothing.

`verify` and `record`: a baseline.json that isn't valid (not JSON, `fingerprints` or `images` `null`
or not an object of objects: `"<key>" must be an object of objects`, an `images` id that isn't a
relative `/`-separated path without `.` or `..` parts) is a usage error. `record`: 2 when the run had errors (images with errors keep their
baseline entry), or when it rendered nothing but would remove baseline images (then nothing
changes); else 0. baseline.json is written last (temp file, then rename).

`accept`: 0 applied (or nothing to apply), 1 refused (the report's commit isn't HEAD and a commit
other than an `accept` commit followed it, `--push` from a fork's pull request, `--push` with HEAD
detached and no branch known, or `git push` failed), 64 usage error or invalid report (also: an
`--only` id the reports don't list, the same id with different content in two reports, a zip entry
leaving the report or a symbolic link, a damaged zip, a `--from` that can't be read, a malformed
manifest.json, result.json or baseline.json, `--branch` without `--push`). Interrupted: 2.

## Serialization

**JSON** (every file on this page):

- Keys sorted by their UTF-8 bytes.
- Pretty: 2-space indent, `"key": value`, one element per line, every non-empty array and
  object expanded (also `[x, y, w, h]` boxes), empty ones as `[]` and `{}`, a final `\n`.
  Compact (used for hashes only): the same with no whitespace at all.
- Strings: escape `"` `\` as `\"` `\\`, LF CR TAB as `\n` `\r` `\t`, other characters below
  U+0020 as `\u00xx` (lowercase hex). Nothing else is escaped (not `/`, not non-ASCII).
- Numbers: an integral value is written as an integer (`1.0` → `1`); others in the shortest
  decimal form that round-trips, never with an exponent (`2.625`, `1.3`). Magnitudes of 1e15 and
  above don't occur in these files (implementations may reject them).
- Arrays of ids or messages are sorted by UTF-8 bytes unless stated otherwise.

**Hash**: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the compact JSON's UTF-8 bytes.

**PNG** (diff images; baseline and new images are byte copies): 8-bit RGBA (colour type 6),
interlace 0, filter type 0 on every row, chunks `IHDR`, one `IDAT`, `IEND` and nothing else. The
`IDAT` is one zlib stream: deflate level 6, window 15, memory level 8, default strategy, as zlib's
`compress2(…, 6)` and Java's `new Deflater(6)` + `finish()` write it (verified identical with zlib
1.2.12). Implementations must use zlib (madler) with these defaults, not zlib-ng.

**Decoding** (for comparison): bit depth 8, colour type 6 (RGBA) or 2 (RGB, alpha 255), any filter,
interlace 0; other chunk types ignored. Samples are used as stored: no colour management, no
premultiplication. Strict: a bad signature, a truncated chunk, a CRC mismatch, `IHDR` missing or
not first, a zlib error, decompressed data of the wrong length or a filter byte above 4 is
malformed. Any other or malformed PNG is the error `unsupported PNG` for that id.

**Determinism**: `commit`, `branch`, `version` and `ci` come from `SWIFTSHOT_COMMIT`,
`SWIFTSHOT_BRANCH`, `SWIFTSHOT_VERSION_OVERRIDE` and `SWIFTSHOT_CI` (`true`/`false`) when set (tests
set them: `0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567`, `feature/x`, `1.0.0-test`, `false`).
Otherwise from CI detection (see CI detection), git and the binary; an unknown commit or branch is `null`. The host is
detected once per run (`SWIFTSHOT_HOST` overrides it) and written into every fingerprint of
that run.

## swiftshot-report.json additions

The run report keeps its current keys and gains:

- `fingerprint`: platform → fingerprint (below), one per platform the run rendered.
- `scope`: what the run covered.
  ```json
  {"platforms": ["android", "ios"], "modules": [":app"], "runtimes": ["26.0"],
   "devices": ["iPhone 17 Pro", "Pixel 9"], "languages": ["en-US"], "appearances": ["dark", "light"],
   "textSizes": ["default"], "fontScales": [1, 1.3], "previews": ["Home", "Settings"],
   "previewFilter": ["Home*"]}
  ```
  Each list is the **requested matrix ∪ the values actually rendered**. Requested: the platforms,
  Gradle modules (Android, desktop), devices, languages, appearances, font scales / text sizes and
  iOS runtime versions the run selected, from flags, the config's global lists and every value
  named in a `screens` rule (resolved: `"ios_versions": ["26"]` → the installed `26.x` versions).
  A selected value counts even when it rendered nothing (a module with no previews, a device only
  a deleted preview used). `modules` and `runtimes` are always present, `[]` when they don't
  apply. `textSizes` when iOS was in the run (`"default"` = the device's own), `fontScales` when
  Android, desktop or Flutter was. `previews`: the preview names the run found after filters
  (informational). `previewFilter`: the `--previews` globs, `[]` when none. All lists sorted
  (`fontScales` by value).
- Per screenshot: `id`, `platform` (`ios`, `android`, `desktop`, `flutter`) and `scale` (pixels per
  point/dp, e.g. `3`, `2.625`). Existing per-screenshot keys used here: `preview`, `device`,
  `language`, `appearance`, `module` (Android, desktop), `fontScale` (Android, desktop, Flutter),
  `textSize` (iOS, absent = `"default"`), `runtime` (iOS). New: `renderer` (Flutter: `impeller`,
  `skia` or `exact-ios`, what rendered this screenshot).
- `errors` become objects: `{"id": "<id>", "message": "…"}`, the id being the one the failed shot
  would have had. An error the run can't tie to a shot (e.g. a module that doesn't compile) has
  no `id`. Several errors for one id: the first in report order counts, the rest are ignored.

`screenshots` and `errors` must be arrays when present; anything else is an error
(`swiftshot-report.json in <dir>: "screenshots" must be an array`, exit 2).

The verify inputs are the report's `screenshots`, `errors`, `scope` and `fingerprint`; the output
directory is not listed.

## Fingerprint

| field | platforms | |
|---|---|---|
| `platform` | all | `ios`, `android`, `desktop`, `flutter` |
| `host` | all | `macos-arm64`, `macos-x64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64` |
| `swiftshot` | all | version |
| `mode` | all | `no-boot`, `device` (iOS); `headless` (Android, desktop, Flutter); `exact-ios` (Flutter, when the iOS engine rendered every image) |
| `xcode` | ios | Xcode's build (`17A400`) |
| `runtimes` | ios, run only | each simulator runtime the run used, version → build (`{"26.5": "23F77"}`) |
| `runtime` | ios, image only | the build of the image's own runtime (`23F77`) |
| `layoutlib`, `compose`, `jdk` | android | versions from the resolved classpath |
| `skiko`, `compose`, `jdk` | desktop | versions from the resolved classpath |
| `flutter`, `fonts` | flutter | version; sorted font file names |
| `renderers` | flutter, run only | the renderers the run used, sorted (`impeller`, `skia`, `exact-ios`) |
| `renderer` | flutter, image only | the image's own renderer |

Values are strings, `fonts` and `renderers` arrays of strings, `runtimes` an object of strings.

**Image fingerprint**: what produced one image. For a run's iOS fingerprint: the same without
`runtimes`, plus `runtime` = `runtimes[<the image's runtime>]` (left out when the run has no build for
it). For a run's Flutter fingerprint: the same without `renderers`, plus `renderer` = the image's
`renderer` and `mode` = `exact-ios` when that is `exact-ios`, else `headless` (both left as they are
when the image has no `renderer`). Every other fingerprint is the run's as it is. baseline.json stores image fingerprints, so an
image keeps the build of its own runtime and its own renderer, whatever else the run used (an
iPhone that fell back from Flutter's iOS engine to Impeller is a mismatch for that image only). watchOS runtimes
are keyed `watchOS <version>` (`"watchOS 11.0": "22R349"`), and a watch screenshot's `runtime` is
the same string, so iOS and watchOS versions never meet. One run, one host: all platform fingerprints of a
run carry the same `host` (a run with iOS is on macOS). **Fingerprint id**: the first 12 hex digits of the
fingerprint's hash.

**Pixel-relevant**: every field, except `swiftshot` compares only its first two `.`-separated parts
(`1.0.3` = `1.0.0-test`), and `host` is ignored when this run's renderer is the exact iOS one: the
image fingerprint has `platform` `ios` or `renderer` `exact-ios`. A field present on one side only
is a difference (the other shown as `none`).

## baseline.json

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "fingerprints": {"d2d5c0db8687": {"host": "macos-arm64", "mode": "no-boot", "platform": "ios", …}},
  "images": {
    "en-US/iPhone 17 Pro-Home": {"fingerprint": "d2d5c0db8687", "platform": "ios", "device": "iPhone 17 Pro",
      "language": "en-US", "appearance": "light", "preview": "Home", "textSize": "default", "runtime": "26.0", "local": false},
    "en-US/Pixel 9-Home": {"fingerprint": "7d572793275d", "platform": "android", "module": ":app",
      "device": "Pixel 9", "language": "en-US", "appearance": "light", "preview": "Home", "fontScale": 1,
      "local": false}
  }
}
```

- Every image references one entry of `fingerprints` (an image fingerprint, see Fingerprint);
  unreferenced fingerprints are dropped on write. `record` and `accept` store the image fingerprint
  of the run's (`accept`: the manifest's) fingerprint for the image's platform and `runtime`.
- iOS images have `textSize` (`"default"` when none) and `runtime`; Android and desktop `module`
  and `fontScale`; Flutter `fontScale` and `renderer`.
- `local`: `true` when the image was rendered outside CI (`record` on a developer machine;
  `accept` writes `local = (ci == null)` from the manifest).

The baseline set is `images`. A PNG under the baseline directory with no `images` entry is
**stray**: it can't be scope-checked, so it is an error only when its id is in this run's output
(below) or has a render error (then the render error is its entry); otherwise it is ignored and
counted in `strayBaselineFiles`. So `strayBaselineFiles` = stray PNGs whose id is not listed. The stray scan runs whether
or not the run has errors.

## Comparison config

`swiftshot.json` keys (the fixtures' `config.json` holds exactly these):

```json
{"tolerance": {"pixels": 5, "max_channel_delta": 1},
 "screens": [{"preview": "Clock*", "tolerance": {"max_channel_delta": 2}},
             {"preview": "Feed", "ignore_regions": [[0, 0, 16, 4]]}]}
```

- `tolerance.max_channel_delta` d (default 0): a pixel differs when any of R, G, B, A differs by
  more than d. `tolerance.pixels` n (default 0): up to n differing pixels still count as unchanged.
  Both may be set.
- `screens`: the first rule whose `preview` glob matches the preview name applies (as for all
  `screens` keys; glob: `*` = any run of characters, whole name, ASCII case-insensitive). Its
  `tolerance` replaces the global one; its `ignore_regions` apply.
- Without any tolerance for a screenshot (neither the rule nor the global one), a screenshot whose
  platform fingerprint has `mode` `device` uses `{"max_channel_delta": 1}`; all others exact.
- `ignore_regions`: `[x, y, w, h]` in points (iOS) or dp, times the screenshot's `scale`:
  `x0 = floor(x·s)`, `y0 = floor(y·s)`, `x1 = ceil((x+w)·s)`, `y1 = ceil((y+h)·s)` (double
  precision, in that order), clipped to the canvas; pixels with `x0 ≤ x < x1`, `y0 ≤ y < y1` never
  differ.

**configHash**: the hash of the normalized config:
`{"screens": [<every rule in order: "preview", plus "tolerance" and "ignore_regions" when set>], "tolerance": T}`,
every tolerance written with both keys (`{"max_channel_delta": d, "pixels": n}`, absent = 0). Rules
with other keys only appear as `{"preview": …}`. The `mode` default above is not part of it.

## Status

**Ids**: the report's `screenshots`, the report's `errors` with an `id`, baseline.json `images`, and
stray PNGs whose id is in `screenshots`. For each id, in this order:

1. **Leave out** (not listed, not counted, no fingerprint or `local` check): not in `screenshots`,
   no render error, and the baseline image is out of scope or the run has an error without `id`
   (such a run can't tell which shots it lost, so it reports no removals).
2. **`error`**, the first that applies:
   1. render error (report `errors`) → its message
   2. in `screenshots`, no output PNG → `output image missing`
   3. in `images`, no baseline PNG → `baseline image missing`
   4. stray baseline PNG → `baseline image not in baseline.json`
   5. both PNGs present, bytes differ, either not decodable as below → `unsupported PNG`
3. **`removed`**: not in `screenshots`. **`added`**: not in `images`.
4. **`unchanged`**: the PNG bytes are equal (checked before decoding, so equal files are never
   decoded and never `unsupported`).
5. Otherwise compare (below): `unchanged` or `changed`.

`error` is never `removed`, and `accept` never deletes the baseline image of an `error` id.

A run whose report lists no screenshots and no errors is an error, not a mass removal:
`status: "error"`, `errors: [{"message": "The run rendered no screenshots"}]` (an error without
`id`, so removals are suppressed as in step 1; `removed` is 0).

**In scope**: `platform` ∈ `platforms`, `device` ∈ `devices`, `language` ∈ `languages`,
`appearance` ∈ `appearances`; `module` ∈ `modules`, `runtime` ∈ `runtimes`, `textSize` ∈
`textSizes`, `fontScale` ∈ `fontScales`, each if the image has that key; and `previewFilter` is
empty or one of its globs matches `preview`. A list missing from the scope matches nothing.
Strings compare exactly; `fontScale` compares as a decimal value (`1` = `1.0`, `1.3` = `1.30`).

**Comparison** (bytes differ): decode both. Canvas = max width × max height. A canvas pixel
differs when it lies outside either image, or the channel rule says so; then ignore regions are
removed. `pixels` = number of differing pixels.

- Sizes differ → `changed`, reason `size` (always, whatever the tolerance), with `baselineSize`
  and `newSize` `[w, h]`.
- Else `pixels` ≤ n → `unchanged`; reason `tolerance` and `pixels` when `pixels` > 0.
- Else `changed`, reason `pixels`.

**Boxes** (changed only), on the canvas's differing pixels: 8-connected components, each as its
bounding box, half-open `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)`. Two boxes are close when
`max(0, b.x0−a.x1, a.x0−b.x1, b.y0−a.y1, a.y0−b.y1) < 16`; replace any close pair by its union
until no pair is close (the result does not depend on the order). Written as `[x, y, w, h]`,
sorted by y, x, w, h.

**Diff image** (changed only), canvas-sized, opaque: a differing pixel is `#FF2D55`; any other
pixel inside the baseline is the baseline at 30 % over white; the rest is white. With baseline
sample c and alpha a (0–255), in integers:
`c1 = (c·a + 255·(255−a) + 127) / 255`, `out = (3·c1 + 7·255 + 5) / 10` (`/` truncates), alpha 255.

**Errors**: `errors` holds `{"id", "message"}` for every `error` entry (sorted by id), then the
report's errors without `id` as `{"message"}`, in report order.

**Fingerprint mismatch**: for every listed id with an `images` entry (any status, `error` included),
compare that entry's fingerprint with the image fingerprint this run gives it: the run's fingerprint
for its platform (none: skipped) made an image fingerprint (see Fingerprint) for this run's
screenshot of that id, or for the entry itself when the run has none (removed, error).
Each pixel-relevant difference is a message `<platform> <field>: baseline <value>, this run <value>`
(arrays joined with `, `, absent = `none`); duplicates dropped, sorted. `verify` prints these
first; they never change the status.

**localBaseline**: `true` when the `images` entry of a listed id (any status, `error` included) has
`local: true`. A warning, never a failure.

## CI detection

The environment is read once at start-up and passed down; nothing below reads it again. An empty
value counts as unset.

1. `SWIFTSHOT_CI` set to anything but `true` or `1` (case-insensitive), `false` included: not a CI.
   Every `ci` field is `null`, whatever else is set.
2. The first row of the table below whose condition holds names the provider.
3. No row holds but `SWIFTSHOT_CI` or `CI` is `true` or `1`: a CI of unknown provider
   (`provider: null`, every other field `null`).
4. Otherwise not a CI.

| provider | detected when | commit (first non-empty) | branch | pullRequest | fork | buildUrl | repository |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `github` | `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` | `pull_request.head.sha` of the JSON file at `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`, else `GITHUB_SHA` | `GITHUB_HEAD_REF`, else `GITHUB_REF_NAME` when `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` is `push` and `GITHUB_REF_TYPE` isn't `tag` | `pull_request.number` of that file | `pull_request.head.repo.full_name` differs from `pull_request.base.repo.full_name` (both present) | `$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$GITHUB_RUN_ID` | `$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY` |
| `gitlab` | `GITLAB_CI=true` | `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_SOURCE_BRANCH_SHA`, else `CI_COMMIT_SHA` | `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_SOURCE_BRANCH_NAME`, else `CI_COMMIT_BRANCH` | `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_IID` | `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_SOURCE_PROJECT_ID` differs from `CI_MERGE_REQUEST_PROJECT_ID` (both set) | `CI_JOB_URL` | `CI_PROJECT_URL` |
| `bitbucket` | `BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER` set | `BITBUCKET_COMMIT` | `BITBUCKET_BRANCH` | `BITBUCKET_PR_ID` | `false` on a pull request (fork pull requests run no pipeline), else `null` | `$BITBUCKET_GIT_HTTP_ORIGIN/pipelines/results/$BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER` | `BITBUCKET_GIT_HTTP_ORIGIN` |
| `bitrise` | `BITRISE_IO=true` | `BITRISE_GIT_COMMIT`, else `GIT_CLONE_COMMIT_HASH` | `BITRISE_GIT_BRANCH` | `BITRISE_PULL_REQUEST` | `BITRISEIO_PULL_REQUEST_REPOSITORY_URL` differs from `GIT_REPOSITORY_URL` (both set) | `BITRISE_BUILD_URL` | `GIT_REPOSITORY_URL` |
| `codemagic` | `CM_BUILD_ID` set | `CM_COMMIT` | `CM_BRANCH` | `CM_PULL_REQUEST_NUMBER` | `null` | `null` | `null` |
| `circleci` | `CIRCLECI=true` | `CIRCLE_SHA1` | `CIRCLE_BRANCH` | last path segment of `CIRCLE_PULL_REQUEST` | `true` if `CIRCLE_PR_NUMBER` is set (only forks set it), else `false` if `CIRCLE_PULL_REQUEST` is set, else `null` | `CIRCLE_BUILD_URL` | `CIRCLE_REPOSITORY_URL` |
| `azure` | `TF_BUILD=true` (case-insensitive) | `SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_SOURCECOMMITID`, else `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION` | `SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_SOURCEBRANCH` without `refs/heads/`, else `BUILD_SOURCEBRANCH` without `refs/heads/`, else `BUILD_SOURCEBRANCHNAME` | `SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_PULLREQUESTNUMBER`, else `SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_PULLREQUESTID` | `SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_ISFORK` (`True`/`False`, case-insensitive), else `null` | `$SYSTEM_COLLECTIONURI$SYSTEM_TEAMPROJECT/_build/results?buildId=$BUILD_BUILDID` (one `/` after the collection URI) | `BUILD_REPOSITORY_URI` |
| `jenkins` | `JENKINS_URL` set | `GIT_COMMIT` | `CHANGE_BRANCH`, else `BRANCH_NAME`, else `GIT_BRANCH` without `origin/` | `CHANGE_ID` | `true` if `CHANGE_FORK` is set, else `false` if `CHANGE_ID` is set, else `null` | `BUILD_URL` | `GIT_URL` |

A field whose variables are not all set is `null`. `pullRequest` is a string (`"7"`). `repository` is
the clone URL or slug the CI gives; it is not written to a report, `Host` uses it only when the git
remote is unusable. The azure collection URI ends in `/` in practice.

Then `commit = SWIFTSHOT_COMMIT`, else the CI's commit, else `git rev-parse HEAD`; `branch =
SWIFTSHOT_BRANCH`, else the CI's branch, else the current git branch (none when detached).

**GitHub event file.** Read through the process's working directory (a relative path) or as given.
A missing, unreadable or malformed file (not a JSON object) is not an error: `commit` falls back to
`GITHUB_SHA`, `pullRequest` and `fork` are `null`, and the warning `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH unreadable;
recording GITHUB_SHA, which is a merge commit on pull requests` is printed. A file without a
`pull_request` object (a `push`) is fine and gives no warning; so does an unset `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH`.

**Recorded but not derived.** Some CIs check out a merge commit and say nothing reliable about the
source commit, so a recipe sets `SWIFTSHOT_COMMIT` itself:
- GitHub `pull_request` checkouts are `refs/pull/N/merge`, and `GITHUB_SHA` is that merge commit;
  the head commit is only in the event payload
  ([events](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows),
  [variables](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/variables)).
- Jenkins multibranch with the "merge" discovery strategy builds a synthetic merge commit, and `GIT_COMMIT`
  may be it (JENKINS-62783, https://issues.jenkins.io/browse/JENKINS-62783; strategies:
  https://docs.cloudbees.com/docs/cloudbees-ci/latest/multibranch-pipeline-template-syntax-guide/github).
- Bitbucket pull request pipelines merge the destination branch before the run, and the docs do not say
  whether `BITBUCKET_COMMIT` is the source tip
  (https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/pipeline-start-conditions/).
- Bitrise (`merge_pr` default) and Codemagic may check out a merge; neither documents which commit
  `BITRISE_GIT_COMMIT` / `CM_COMMIT` is on that checkout.
- Azure Repos and GitHub pull request builds use the merge commit as `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION`; the source
  commit is `SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_SOURCECOMMITID`, which is why it comes first.
- Azure `BUILD_SOURCEBRANCHNAME` is only the last path segment (`feature/tools` gives `tools`), so the
  full `BUILD_SOURCEBRANCH` is used first.

Sources of the variables: GitHub https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/variables ·
GitLab https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/variables/predefined_variables/ ·
Bitbucket https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/variables-and-secrets/ ·
Bitrise https://docs.bitrise.io/en/bitrise-ci/references/available-environment-variables.html ·
Codemagic https://docs.codemagic.io/yaml-basic-configuration/environment-variables/ ·
CircleCI https://circleci.com/docs/reference/variables/ ·
Azure https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/build/variables ·
Jenkins https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/pipeline/jenkinsfile/ and https://www.jenkins.io/doc/book/pipeline/multibranch/.
On Codemagic `CM_BRANCH` is the pull request's source branch (https://docs.codemagic.io/yaml-basic-configuration/environment-variables/).

Fixtures: `Shared/testdata/ci/` (one file per case) and the baseline case `ci-github`.

## result.json

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "status": "failed",
  "counts": {"added": 0, "changed": 1, "errors": 0, "removed": 0, "unchanged": 1},
  "commit": "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567",
  "branch": "feature/x",
  "version": "1.0.0-test",
  "ci": null,
  "host": "linux-x64",
  "fingerprint": {"android": {…}},
  "fingerprintMismatch": [],
  "localBaseline": false,
  "screenshots": [
    {"id": "en-US/Pixel 9-Home", "status": "changed", "reason": "pixels", "pixels": 62,
     "boxes": [[5, 5, 4, 18], [20, 40, 1, 1], [28, 60, 6, 6]],
     "baseline": "images/baseline/en-US/Pixel 9-Home.png", "new": "images/new/en-US/Pixel 9-Home.png",
     "diff": "images/diff/en-US/Pixel 9-Home.png",
     "platform": "android", "module": ":app", "device": "Pixel 9", "language": "en-US",
     "appearance": "light", "preview": "Home", "fontScale": 1},
    {"id": "en-US/Pixel 9-Broken", "status": "error", "message": "IllegalStateException: boom", …}
  ],
  "errors": [{"id": "en-US/Pixel 9-Broken", "message": "IllegalStateException: boom"}],
  "strayBaselineFiles": 0
}
```

- `status`: `error` if `errors` is not empty, else `failed` if any changed/added/removed, else
  `passed`. Exit code 2, 1, 0.
- `counts.errors` = length of `errors` (`error` entries plus errors without id).
- `ci`: `null` when this run was not on a CI (see CI detection), else `{"buildUrl", "provider",
  "pullRequest"}` with sorted keys, each a string or `null` (`provider` is `null` for a CI of unknown
  provider). `fork` and `repository` are not written. `host`: this run's host, the same value as
  `host` in each of its fingerprints; `null` when the run fingerprint is empty. Readers must ignore
  unknown keys.
- `fingerprint`: the run's, as in the report.
- `strayBaselineFiles`: stray baseline PNGs whose id is not listed in `screenshots`.
- `screenshots`: every listed id, sorted by id (UTF-8 bytes). Each has `platform`, `device`,
  `language`, `appearance`, `preview`, `fontScale` or `textSize` (`"default"` when none), `module`
  (Android, desktop) and `runtime` (iOS): every one the report's screenshot entry provides,
  otherwise from the `images` entry (removed, and `error` ids not in `screenshots`); an `error` id
  in neither has only `id`, `status`, `message`. Present only when they apply: `message` (error),
  `reason`,
  `pixels`, `boxes`, `canvasSize`, `baselineSize`, `newSize`, and the image paths (relative to the report
  directory, not URL-encoded): `baseline` (changed, removed), `new` (changed, added), `diff` (changed).
- `canvasSize`: `[w, h]` of the canvas (see Comparison), on every `changed` entry; `pixels` of `w × h`
  is the share that changed. Added without changing `schema`: it stays 1, because readers ignore
  unknown keys and nothing in `accept` reads it.

## index.html

One page for people to read `result.json`: a list by status, the images side by side, on a slider or
as the diff image, filters, and a tray that builds the accept text. It works from `file://` in a
downloaded report: no network, no external files, and a Content-Security-Policy that allows only its
own style and script.

- The page is `Shared/report.html` with one change: `__SWIFTSHOT_RESULT_JSON__` is replaced by the bytes
  of `result.json`, each `<` written as `\u003c`. So the file is the same from both implementations.
  The Swift binary compiles the template in and the JVM jar has it as a resource; there are no copies.
  `make.py` refreshes the policy's hashes, so run it after editing the template.
- `--no-html` (`"html": false` in swiftshot.json) means no HTML from this run: neither
  `screenshots.html` nor `index.html`. Everything else in the report stays.
- Images are referenced only through the paths in `result.json`, each segment percent-encoded.
- A row is ticked to accept it, and the tray builds the text: with `ci.provider` `github`, a `ci.pullRequest` that is not `null` and a `commit` (7 to 64 hex digits)
  the comment: `/swiftshot accept <commit>` with the report's full `commit`, then, when only some rows
  are ticked, the ids one per line. The recipe replies that the report is out of date, and accepts
  nothing, when the commit is not a prefix of the pull request's head; a bare `/swiftshot accept`
  typed by a person accepts the latest run. Otherwise (no pull request, no commit, another CI)
  `swiftshot accept --from <report> --only "<id>,<id>"`,
  single-quoted when an id has `$`, a backtick, `\`, `"` or `!`, with `--from` the page's own folder
  when opened from `file://`. A list over 100,000 bytes is split into repeated `--only` flags (one
  argument may not pass 128 KiB on Linux); over 400,000 bytes in all the tray warns and says to tick
  fewer. The bare form appears only when every changed, added and removed row is
  ticked. "Tick all" ticks only the rows the filters show, and says how many. A row can't be ticked when its id has a comma (`--only` and the comment recipe split or refuse
  on it), a control character or line break, or starts or ends with white space (both trim it). The
  bare form still accepts such a row.
- `index.html` adds nothing that `accept` reads, and is in `swiftshot-report.zip` like every other file.

## manifest.json

In the report directory; `accept` checks it against the branch. `ci`: `null` when the verify run was
not on a CI, else the same object as in result.json; `accept` writes `local = (ci == null)` into the
images it applies. A manifest whose `ci` is neither `null` nor an object is a usage error
(`manifest.json has no ci`). `accept` only touches the ids
listed here, so a baseline image of an `error` id is never deleted.

```json
{"schema": 1, "commit": "…", "branch": "feature/x", "ci": {"buildUrl": "…", "provider": "github", "pullRequest": "7"}, "configHash": "8f36…",
 "fingerprint": {"android": {…}}, "ids": {"added": [], "changed": ["en-US/Pixel 9-Home"], "removed": []}}
```

## accept

`swiftshot accept --from <report> [--from <report>…] [--only <ids>] [--push] [--branch <name>] [--author "Name <email>"]`
renders nothing. `--from` is a report directory, a zip of one (the report at its root or in its only
top-level directory), or an `http(s)` URL of such a zip (sent with `$SWIFTSHOT_ARTIFACT_TOKEN` when
set, only to that host and only over `https`: a token with an `http` URL is a usage error, except to
`localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1`). The header, first that applies:

- `SWIFTSHOT_ARTIFACT_HEADER`, `Name: value` with `{token}` in the value.
- `api.github.com` or the host of `GITHUB_API_URL`: `Authorization: Bearer <t>`.
- `gitlab.com` or the host of `CI_API_V4_URL`: `JOB-TOKEN: <t>` when `<t>` is `CI_JOB_TOKEN`, else `PRIVATE-TOKEN: <t>`.
- `circleci.com`: `Circle-Token: <t>`.
- `dev.azure.com`, `*.visualstudio.com`: `Authorization: Basic base64(":" + <t>)`.
- a `<t>` with a `:` (Jenkins `user:apitoken`): `Authorization: Basic base64(<t>)`.
- otherwise `Authorization: Bearer <t>`.

Bitrise and Codemagic give pre-signed URLs; pass those without a token. Zips: no entry may leave the target
directory or be a symbolic link, at most 2 GB extracted.

- For each `changed` and `added` id of `manifest.json`: `images/new/<id>.png` is copied into the
  baseline; its `images` entry is the report's `result.json` screenshot entry (the fields of the
  baseline.json example), `fingerprint` the id of the manifest's fingerprint for its platform,
  `local` = `(ci == null)`. Each `removed` id: its PNG and entry are deleted. Nothing else changes;
  unreferenced fingerprints are dropped and baseline.json is rewritten canonically.
- `--only` (comma-separated, repeatable) restricts to those ids.
- When every selected change is `removed` (and there is at least one), a warning:
  `Every change in the report is a removal (N screenshots); check the run rendered what you expected`
  ("1 screenshot" for one).
- A report whose `result.json` `status` is `error`: a warning, then its listed ids are applied as
  usual (ids with errors are in none of the lists, so they keep their baseline).
- Stale: each report's `commit` must be HEAD, or every commit after it up to HEAD must carry the
  trailer `Swiftshot-Accept: <commit>` (any value), which `accept --push` writes.
- baseline.json is written last (temp file, then rename).
- `--push`: one commit of only the files accept wrote or deleted (other edits in the baseline
  directory stay uncommitted), subject `Update screenshot baseline (3
  changed, 1 added)` (non-zero parts of changed, added, removed), a `Swiftshot-Accept: <commit>`
  trailer per report commit, author and committer `swiftshot <swiftshot@users.noreply.github.com>`
  unless `--author`; then `git push`, never forced, to the first that applies:
  1. `--branch <name>`: `<remote> HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` (`<remote>` is the upstream's, else `origin`).
  2. The current branch's upstream.
  3. HEAD detached (a CI checkout): `origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, `<branch>` being
     `SWIFTSHOT_BRANCH`, else the CI's branch (`ci.branch`).
  4. Else `origin HEAD`.

  With HEAD detached and no branch known, exit 1: `HEAD is detached and no branch is known; pass
  --branch <the pull request branch>`. When the CI says the pull request comes from a fork (`ci.fork`
  is true), exit 1 before anything is written: `This pull request comes from a fork; download the
  report and run swiftshot accept --from <report> in the fork`. With `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN` set and an
  `https` push remote (or `http` to this machine; see "Git host" for the header) the header goes to
  `git push` alone, in its environment (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>=http.extraHeader`,
  `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>`, after any `GIT_CONFIG_*` entries already set): never on git's command line
  or in the git config, and the token, its base64 form and the header are replaced with `***` in
  git's output and in the refusal message. A token push needs an `https` remote: with an `ssh`, `scp`-style
  or other remote, one warning `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN is not used: <remote> is not an https remote (a
  token push needs one)` and a plain `git push` with git's own credentials.
  Nothing to apply, or none of those files changed: no commit.

## junit.xml

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<testsuite name="swiftshot" tests="4" failures="1" errors="2">
  <testcase classname="android.Pixel 9.en-US" name="en-US/Pixel 9-Broken">
    <error message="IllegalStateException: boom"/>
  </testcase>
  <testcase classname="android.Pixel 9.en-US" name="en-US/Pixel 9-Home">
    <failure message="changed: 62 pixels"/>
  </testcase>
  <testcase classname="android.Pixel 9.en-US" name="en-US/Pixel 9-Settings-1.3x"/>
  <testcase classname="swiftshot" name="error 1">
    <error message=":feature: compilation failed"/>
  </testcase>
</testsuite>
```

- One `<testcase>` per `screenshots` entry, same order, then one per error without id
  (`name="error <n>"`, from 1).
- `classname="<platform>.<device>.<language>"` (`swiftshot` for an `error` id without those
  fields), `name="<id>"`.
- `<failure message=…/>`: `changed: <pixels> pixels`, `changed: size <w>x<h> to <w>x<h>`, `added`,
  `removed`. `<error message="<message>"/>` for errors. Unchanged entries are self-closing.
- `tests` = entries + errors without id, `failures` = changed + added + removed, `errors` =
  `counts.errors`.
- Attribute escaping: `&` `<` `>` `"` as `&amp;` `&lt;` `&gt;` `&quot;`; TAB LF CR as `&#9;`
  `&#10;` `&#13;`; other characters below U+0020 dropped. 2-space indent, LF line ends, final `\n`.

## summary.md

The report in a few lines of Markdown: the CI's summary page, and the pull request comment (the same
text). UTF-8, `\n` line ends, one final `\n`. Blocks are separated by one blank line.

```
<!-- swiftshot -->
### Screenshots differ from the baseline

1 changed · 1 added · 0 removed · 0 errors · 3 unchanged

> **Note:** Baseline rendered differently: android host: baseline linux-x64, this run macos-arm64

| Status | Screenshot | Pixels |
|---|---|---|
| changed | `en-US/Pixel 9-Home` | 1.9% |
| added | `en-US/Pixel 9-New` | |

[Full report](https://github.com/acme/app/actions/runs/9876543210)

Comment `/swiftshot accept` on this pull request to accept every change, or put screenshot ids one per line below it to accept some.
```

- Heading by `status`: `passed` "Screenshots match the baseline", `failed` "Screenshots differ from
  the baseline", `error` "Screenshot run had errors".
- Counts line: all five counts, in the order above, separated by ` · ` (U+00B7).
- Note block: one `> **Note:** ` line per `fingerprintMismatch` entry (`Baseline rendered differently:
  <entry>`), then, when `localBaseline`, `Some baseline images were recorded outside CI (local);
  record or accept them on CI`. Omitted when empty.
- Table: one row per `error`, `changed`, `added` or `removed` entry, in that status order, then by id
  in UTF-8 byte order; at most 200 rows, then `| | …and <n> more | |`. In an id, `|` is written `\|`
  and a backtick `'`. Omitted when there are no rows. Errors without id have no row (see the counts).
- `Pixels`: for `changed` rows, `pixels` as a share of `canvasSize`; blank (`| |`) for other rows. In
  integers, so both implementations agree: `<0.1%` when `pixels > 0` and `pixels · 1000 < w · h`; `>99.9%` when `pixels < w · h` and
  `pixels · 1000 > w · h · 999` (so only a canvas that changed entirely reads `100.0%`); else
  `t = (pixels · 2000 + w · h) / (2 · w · h)` (`/` truncates) written as `<t / 10>.<t % 10>%`. In the
  table the cell is written `\>99.9%`, so Markdown shows the `>` literally; `index.html` shows `>99.9%`.
- `[Full report](<ci.buildUrl>)`: when `ci.buildUrl` is set, for every status, after the table. It links
  to the CI's build, where the report directory is kept: download it and open `index.html`.
- Accept hint, `failed` only, last. By `ci.provider`; `null` or unknown gets the last text:
  - `github`: Comment `/swiftshot accept` on this pull request to accept every change, or put screenshot ids one per line below it to accept some.
  - `gitlab`: Run the manual `swiftshot-accept` job in this pipeline to accept the changes.
  - `bitbucket`: Run the `swiftshot-accept` custom pipeline on this branch to accept the changes.
  - `bitrise`: Run the `swiftshot-accept` workflow on this branch to accept the changes.
  - `codemagic`: Start the `swiftshot-accept` workflow on this branch to accept the changes.
  - `circleci`: Approve the `accept-screenshots` job in this workflow to accept the changes.
  - `azure`: Approve the `Accept screenshots` stage in this run to accept the changes.
  - `jenkins`: Approve the `Accept screenshots` stage in this build to accept the changes.
  - otherwise: Accept the changes with `swiftshot accept --from <this report>`.
- Size: the text stays within 60,000 UTF-8 bytes (GitHub allows 65,536 characters). If it is larger,
  rows are dropped from the end until it fits; the "…and <n> more" count includes them.

## Native CI output

After `verify` has written the report, it adds what the detected CI (`ci.provider`) reads. `verify`
takes the process environment as given; with `SWIFTSHOT_CI=false` nothing is written. Each part needs
its variable; a write that fails is one warning and never changes the exit code.

- `github`: appends `summary.md` to the file `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Prints to stdout, for the first
  10 table rows, `::error title=<status> screenshot::<id>`, and for an `error` row
  `::error title=Render error::<id>: <message>`. Values escape `%` `\r` `\n` as `%25` `%0D` `%0A`, a
  title also `:` `,` as `%3A` `%2C`.
- `azure`: prints `##vso[results.publish type=JUnit;mergeResults=false;runTitle=swiftshot;resultFiles=<absolute junit.xml>]`
  and `##vso[task.uploadsummary]<absolute summary.md>`; when `status` is not `passed` also
  `##vso[task.logissue type=error]Screenshots: <counts line>`.
- `bitbucket`: copies `junit.xml` to `$BITBUCKET_CLONE_DIR/test-results/swiftshot/junit.xml`.
- `bitrise`: with `BITRISE_TEST_RESULT_DIR`, writes `swiftshot/junit.xml` and `swiftshot/test-info.json`
  (`{"test-name":"swiftshot"}`) there; with `BITRISE_DEPLOY_DIR`, writes `swiftshot-report.zip` there:
  the report directory's files at the zip's root (what `accept --from` reads), entries sorted by name,
  every timestamp 1980-01-01 00:00.
- `gitlab`, `codemagic`, `circleci`, `jenkins`: nothing; their recipes point at `junit.xml` and the
  report directory.

## Git host

After the native CI output, `verify` comments its `summary.md` on the pull request. It needs
`SWIFTSHOT_HOST_TOKEN`, a CI run for a pull request (`ci.pullRequest`) and a known host; without the
token or the pull request it does nothing. The host comes from `git remote get-url origin` in the
repository containing the project directory (`https://[user@]host[:port]/a/b[.git]`,
`ssh://git@host[:port]/a/b[.git]`, `git@host:a/b[.git]`):

| host | when | API | token header |
|---|---|---|---|
| `github` | `github.com`; or the host of `GITHUB_SERVER_URL` in GitHub Actions (GitHub Enterprise) | `https://api.github.com`; `GITHUB_API_URL` in Actions; else `https://<host>/api/v3` | `Authorization: Bearer <t>` |
| `gitlab` | `gitlab.com`; or the host of `CI_API_V4_URL` | `CI_API_V4_URL` (when it is the same host), else `https://<host>/api/v4` | `PRIVATE-TOKEN: <t>` |
| `bitbucket` | `bitbucket.org` | `https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0` | `Authorization: Bearer <t>`, or `Basic base64(<t>)` when `<t>` contains `:` (`email:api-token`) |

`SWIFTSHOT_GIT_HOST` (`github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`) names the host kind, and `SWIFTSHOT_HOST_API` the
API base; when set, each wins over what the remote says (`SWIFTSHOT_HOST` is the renderer host of the
fingerprint and is not used here). A GitLab project path keeps its subgroups and is URL-encoded in API paths. An unknown
host sends nothing and prints one line (never the token). A GitLab job token can't write notes: use a
project or personal access token with the `api` scope.

The comment body is exactly `summary.md`, whose first line is `<!-- swiftshot -->`. The first comment
whose text starts with that line is updated (GitHub `PATCH`, GitLab and Bitbucket `PUT`); else one is
created. At most 10 pages of 100 comments are read: GitHub and GitLab go on while a page has 100,
Bitbucket while its page has `next`. A comment whose `id` isn't a whole number that fits 64 bits is
skipped.

| host | list and create | update | text |
|---|---|---|---|
| `github` | `{api}/repos/{project}/issues/{pr}/comments?per_page=100&page=N` | `…/issues/comments/{id}` | `body` |
| `gitlab` | `{api}/projects/{project, / as %2F}/merge_requests/{pr}/notes?per_page=100&page=N&sort=asc` | `…/notes/{id}` | `body` |
| `bitbucket` | `{api}/repositories/{project}/pullrequests/{pr}/comments?pagelen=100&page=N` | `…/comments/{id}` | `content.raw` |

The token is sent only over `https` (or to this machine) and never along a redirect: a 3xx is a
failure, not followed. Any failure (a status other than 2xx, no reply, a reply that isn't the expected
JSON, a non-https API) is one warning, `couldn't comment on the pull request (<host> <status>)`
